people.biography:
Abdelrahman Hassan is a Principal at Enza Capital,  a venture fund investing in early-stage African technology companies solving large and meaningful problems  Enza Capital is based out of Nairobi Kenya, has made 50 investments to date through its Fund I & Fund II, and is managing +$60m across its investment vehicles. Abdelrahman leads Enza’s investments in North Africa, with a focus on Morocco, Egypt, and Tunisia, and plays a key role in sourcing, evaluating, and supporting high-growth technology businesses across fintech, proptech, logistics, healthcare, climate and AI. He currently serves on the Boards of WideBot, Tuteria, and Hub2.

Prior to Enza Capital, Abdelrahman was an Associate at the Omidyar Network in Kenya where he focused on driving strategy and investments in ed-tech innovations across Africa, Latin America and the United States. Abdelrahman started his career at Dalberg Capital, an impact investing advisory firm, working to align capital with meaning and increase capital flows in impact investing. Abdelrahman has a BSc in Financial Economics from the University of Rochester, along with an MSc in Sustainable Finance from the Frankfurt School of Finance.

people.biography:
Abdulaziz Elgammal is the Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer at Proteinea, an AI-native drug development company building an “evergreen” engine for therapeutic asset creation, with a core focus on engineering next generation antibody therapeutics. He works at the intersection of deep tech and biotech, translating frontier AI capabilities into real-world R&D products, partnerships, and investable pipelines.

At Proteinea, Abdulaziz leads product strategy and execution across platform development and partner-facing programs. His work focuses on building repeatable, de-risked systems that can continuously generate high-value therapeutic candidates, helping position the company as a long-term biotech powerhouse in the MEA region.

He is passionate about how capital, incentives, and product thinking shape the trajectory of deep tech startups, especially in domains where timelines are long, technical risk is real, and the reward is outsized impact. When he’s not thinking about molecules and models, you’ll likely find him in Cairo hunting for a great coffee, taking long city walks, and collecting stories from founders who are brave enough to build the future early.

sessions.title: The Funding Blind Spot: Are Deeptech Startups Overlooked?

people.biography:
Dr. Ahmed Al-Qatatsheh leads the quantum business, including quantum strategy formulation and development, as well as quantum computing and research collaboration for IBM Quantum in the Middle East and Africa. Dr. Ahmed is an IBM Senior Quantum Ambassador and QISKIT Advocate, as well as a leading researcher in material science, nanotechnology, and quantum computing. Furthermore, Dr. Ahmed is affiliated with numerous local and international universities and research centers, in addition to serving on scientific advisory boards. His research focuses on practical applications in aerospace, automotive, defense, healthcare, and sustainability. Dr. Ahmed aims to address real-world challenges using material science, quantum technology, and nanoscale innovations. With a strong track record in academia and industry, Dr. Ahmed has conducted collaborative research with renowned institutions, including the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO), the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), and the Innovative Manufacturing CRC (IMCRC). Before working with IBM, Ahmed worked for renowned international companies in the areas of Automotive, Electric Vehicle, and Consulting. 
Dr. Ahmed has made significant contributions to advancing quantum computing, particularly in addressing computational challenges and exploring new architectures and algorithms in materials science for superconductivity and other material properties. His research in nanotechnology has enabled various applications, including sensing and actuation, as well as carbon capture solutions, that offer innovative approaches to mitigating climate change.
Ahmed’s passion for STEM education and Industry 4.0 is evident in his advocacy for international collaboration and knowledge exchange. He has led discussions and delivered presentations to senior executives and policymakers, informing their strategic decisions for the smooth adoption of advanced technologies and building eco-systems for innovation. Ahmed’s commitment to mentoring future scientists and innovators ensures his work remains relevant and impactful in the ever-evolving technological landscape. Dr. Ahmed has a strong publication record, including several high-impact articles in top-tier journals, as well as book chapters and conference papers.

Egyptian Actor, theater director and Improv coach. He began his artistic journey in 2008 through numerous stage productions. He trained under a variety of esteemed Egyptian and international coaches in acting, improvisation, movement, and voice, which helped him refine his craft and expand his performance range.

His artistic work spans across theatre, television drama, films, TV shows, radio, hosting, and advertising — making him a versatile and well-rounded performer.

He is one of the co-founders of the interactive theatre troupe “Maktoob ‘Alina”, which created and performed the first improvised interactive theatre show of its kind in the Middle East, pioneering a new space for live improvisational performance in the region.

Since joining Improv Theatre, he has performed in over 50 live improv show.

He was honored to represent Egypt as an actor in the East-West Dialogue fellowship program to the USA  and last year i had a a Meisner technique training with James Price founder of the Acting Studio NewYork.

On the professional acting side, during 2025 he played some significant roles as an actor Like Dessouki in El Set movie directed by Marwan Hamed, the TV series Single Mother Father and El Sada El Afadl movie and he is also expecting his new project next Ramadan 2026 like El Nos 2 and Aard wi Talab TV series. 

He also had a 14 years’ experience in the field of Human Resources and he is a Certified personality & ability assessor from SHL, and in 2024 he ended his corporate career as the Head of Talent Management team at one of the biggest financial institutions in Egypt to be a full time artist.

Akram Marwan is a distinguished Career Development and Business Innovation professional with over seventeen years of experience across the FMCG, international development, and HR technology sectors. His career includes key roles at Procter & Gamble and the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), before he transitioned in 2017 from the corporate world to entrepreneurship — channeling his expertise into building ventures that bridge the gap between education and employment.

He currently serves as the Co-Founder and CEO of iCareer, Egypt’s leading career-tech and edtech company, dedicated to empowering youth and early-career professionals through collaborations with ministries, universities, development funds, and top employers. Akram is also the Founder of Recruitera, an AI-powered applicant tracking system designed to manage end-to-end recruitment operations, optimize hiring processes, and enable organizations to make data-driven talent decisions.

He successfully spun off two ventures from iCareer prior to the current acquisition: Qualiphi, a career services management platform, and Vezloo, a provider of international outsourcing services for AI and data annotation

He holds an engineering degree and a Master’s in Innovation and Entrepreneurship from the American University in Cairo, combining technical acumen with a deep commitment to innovation, human capital development, and the future of work.

people.biography:
I come from a finance background, but I’ve never believed numbers should live in spreadsheets alone. For me, finance is a tool to help ideas grow, businesses scale and people turn ambition into something real.
I’m naturally curious and drawn to entrepreneurship for what it represents: creativity, problem-solving and impact. I enjoy being around builders, people who ask hard questions, challenge the status quo and aren’t afraid to start from scratch.
Outside of work, you’ll find me watching (or debating) football, getting lost in a good movie, or exploring history and how it shapes the world today. I stay closely tuned to global news and innovation, not out of habit, but out of genuine interest in how the world is evolving.
At my core, I try to lead with curiosity and generosity. I enjoy sharing knowledge, making connections, and creating value wherever I can without keeping score. If something I do helps someone move forward, that’s more than enough for me.

people.biography:
Ali Mokhtar currently serves as CEO of Beltone Venture Capital (BVC) - a wholly owned subsidiary of Beltone Holding. Mokhtar brings to the role over 14 years of experience in the non-bank financial sector in Egypt and the MENA region.
Mokhtar’s journey in the financial industry began at Beltone, where he held several positions between 2010 and 2020 in Corporate Finance and Asset Management. His experience includes serving as Director and Head of Equity at both Beltone Asset Management and EFG Hermes Asset Management. In his capacity, he was responsible for formulating the strategy for all mandates investing in Egypt. He was responsible for managing c.EGP 7 billion in AUMs ranging from equity funds, balanced funds, portfolios for sovereign entities, and high-net-worth-individual portfolios. In addition, he was responsible for research coverage of various sectors across the MENA region.
Furthermore, Mokhtar assisted a number of Egyptian startups across various sectors during their pre-seed and seed fundraising rounds in his role as consultant and part of their advisory boards — raising more than USD 45 million in necessary capital to fuel their growth and success. In June 2022, Mokhtar played a crucial advisory role to Talabeya (an FMCG B2B e-commerce platform) in its successful acquisition by MNT-Halan.
In recognition of his impact on the VC sector, Mokhtar was recognized by Forbes Middle East as One of Forbes Middle East’s Top Venture Capitalists of 2024.
Mokhtar holds an Executive MBA from London Business School and a dual Master’s degree in Finance from Antwerp Management School and Fordham Gabelli School of Business.

Alicia Iannacone is an international sports presenter and football content creator, widely recognized as one of the leading voices in digital sports media in the Middle East. She was awarded Best Sports Content Creator in the Middle East by the TikTok Awards, reflecting her impact, credibility, and reach across global football audiences.

Passionate about football, media innovation, and female representation in sports, Alicia believes the future of sports storytelling lies in real access, real emotion, and real connection with fans.

When she’s not at a stadium or on set, Alicia enjoys traveling, discovering new cultures through football, and turning everyday moments into stories worth sharing.

people.biography:
Amal Dokhan is a Managing Partner at 500 Global, where she leads seed-stage investments across the MENA region and oversees the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator fund. Her work spans startup investments, ecosystem development, and corporate innovation. Through the fund, she supports founders with capital, mentorship, global networks, access to regional markets, and introductions to investors and strategic partners.
A seasoned ecosystem builder, Amal is also an active angel investor with 14 startups in her personal portfolio. She has been instrumental in shaping the entrepreneurial landscape in Saudi Arabia and the MENA region, working with founders from ideation to market entry and designing innovation programs for organizations such as Dow Chemicals, Zain, Nestlé, and Nissan Infiniti, while consulting across the MENA region, South Africa, and the United States.
Prior to joining 500 Global, Amal served as the Managing Director of the Babson Global Center for Entrepreneurial Leadership and previously was the Manager of Learning and Design at the Entrepreneurship Center at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), where she co-designed and led the New Ventures/TAQADAM accelerator and KAUST’s corporate innovation programs. Earlier at KAUST, she also contributed to the Seed Fund’s marketing and events while supporting early-stage startups. Amal began her career co-founding a tech startup in the UAE and working in media agencies.
Amal serves on the boards of organizations such as Wayakit Company, Cranfield University (UK), and King Abdulaziz University. She writes a monthly column on innovation and entrepreneurship for Leaders Magazine and has spoken at global platforms including the World Economic Forum in Davos, TEDx KAUST, and the Islamic Development Bank Annual Conference.
She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Education, English Language & Literature from King Abdulaziz University and a Master’s in Strategic Marketing and Marketing Management from the University of Wollongong.

people.biography:
Amina Khalil is one of Egypt’s most influential artistic voices of her generation, an actress whose work consistently bridges popular success with purpose-driven storytelling. Through a career defined by courage, range, and emotional depth, she has reshaped expectations of what contemporary Arab drama can explore and whom it can speak for.

She first captured wide attention with her breakout role in the internationally streamed series Grand Hotel, where her commanding presence marked the arrival of a major talent. Since then, Amina Khalil has built a body of work that moves fluidly between film and television, comedy and drama, entertainment and impact. Her performances in films such as Wesh x Wesh have earned both box-office success and strong audience acclaim.

What truly defines Amina Khalil’s career, however, is her fearless choice to tell stories that matter. Through groundbreaking television series such as Leih La?! and Khally Balak Men Zizi, she brought visibility to women’s autonomy and ADHD. Subjects long considered taboo in mainstream media. Her most recent work continues this bold trajectory. In the acclaimed 2025 series Lam Shamseya, the hit ramadan series confronting child abuse, she delivered a deeply human performance that ignited national dialogue and earned her the Murex d’Or for Best Arab Actress in Egyptian Drama.

Beyond the screen, Amina Khalil is a committed advocate for women’s and girls’ rights. She uses her platform to amplify voices, challenge silence, and inspire change embodying a new generation of artists who lead not only with talent, but with purpose.

عمرو عوض الله هو رائد أعمال في مجال التكنولوجيا وخبير تقنيات في الذكاء الاصطناعي. مؤخرًا شغل عمرو منصب الرئيس التنفيذي المؤسِّس لشركة فيكتارا حيث قاد الشركة منذ تأسيسها وخلال سنواتها الأربع الأولى، وبنى نظام تشغيل الوكلاء الموثوق لمساعدة المؤسسات على نشر أنظمة ذكاء اصطناعي مؤسسية موثوقة—مرتكزة على البيانات، ومحكومة بضوابط الحوكمة، وآمنة—للاستخدام الإنتاجي على نطاق واسع
سبق لد. عمرو أن شغل منصب نائب الرئيس لعلاقات المطورين في جوجل كلاود. وقبل انضمامه إلى جوجل في نوفمبر 2019، شارك في تأسيس كلوديرا عام 2008، وبصفته المدير التقني العالمي أمضى 11 عامًا يعمل عن قرب مع مؤسسات حول العالم حول كيفية إدخال البيانات الضخمة واستخلاص القيمة منها. طرحت كلوديرا أسهمها للاكتتاب العام في عام 2017 في بورصة نيويورك ، ثم استحوذت عليها شركة ك.ك.ر. في عام 2021 مقابل 5.3 مليار دولار
كما شغل د. عمرو منصب نائب الرئيس لهندسة ذكاء المنتجات في ياهو! خلال الفترة 2000–2008. وانضم عمرو إلى ياهو بعد استحواذها على شركته الناشئة الأولى ابتيفيا في عام 2000، والتي طوّرت محرك بحث لمعلومات المنتجات عبر الإنترنت
حصل د. عمرو على درجة الدكتوراه في الهندسة الكهربائية من جامعة ستانفورد، وعلى درجتي البكالوريوس والماجستير من جامعة القاهرة في مصر
وفي عام 2021، كان عمرو واحدًا من عشرة علماء وتقنيين بارزين مُنحوا الجنسية الفخرية للمملكة العربية السعودية

with people building for real change.

people.biography:
Amr El Abd is a leading figure in entrepreneurship, venture capital, and innovation policy across emerging markets, with over 25 years of experience. In 2024, he was appointed Advisor to the Prime Minister of Egypt for Entrepreneurship, where he plays a central role in shaping national strategy to empower founders and drive innovation-led growth. In 2025, Amr was appointed to the Board of Directors of MSMEDA, reinforcing his role in advancing Egypt’s SME and entrepreneurship landscape.

He currently serves as Regional Managing Director for MENA at Endeavor, the world’s leading network supporting high-impact entrepreneurs in 46+ markets. In 2022, he served as the CEO of Endeavor Egypt, where he led a major transformation before taking on the regional role in 2023.

Alongside his work at Endeavor, Amr also served as a Senior Advisor to the World Bank, where he supported the design and structuring of Egypt’s first fund-of-funds program, helping mobilize institutional capital to fuel the country’s startup ecosystem.

Previously, Amr was the founding CEO and Vice Chairman of Egypt Ventures, Egypt’s first government-backed VC firm, and the founding Chairman of Falak Startups, one of the region’s largest accelerators. He has also advised the Ministry of Investment on national startup and innovation policy.

A serial entrepreneur and investor, Amr has co-founded and scaled ventures across technology, logistics, consulting, and education. In 2004, he launched the Entrepreneurs Business Forum – Egypt (EBF), the country’s first nonprofit dedicated to empowering entrepreneurs.

He holds a degree in Economics from Georgetown University.

I joined the women’s rowing national team in 2016, broke some national and world records on the rowing machine and decided this is a sport worth sharing with the world through Rowin. I started Rowin in 2018 to make rowing accessible and enjoyable to everyone, not just competitively.  One thing that inspired all this, is my belief that movement is therapy. I believe in the power of sport and movement and its complete relevance to our mental health nowadays. But it cannot happen without enjoying it. Sports and movement should be fun to be sustainable. I continue to be a personal trainer while being a World Rowing certified rowing coach.

sessions.title: Finding your Fit: Inside Different Paths to Fitness

people.biography:
I’m a media professional who lives for good stories, bold ideas, and conversations that actually mean something. I work as a Media Executive Producer and Producer, creating and shaping content across television, digital platforms, and live formats—from the first spark of an idea to seeing it come to life on screen.

I’m also the creator and host of The 30 Show, an online talk show built around one core belief: there’s no such thing as “too late.” The show dives into real, honest conversations about life, work, passions, and the messy in-between, featuring guests from different backgrounds and industries. Think less textbook advice, more real talk.

What excites me most is building ideas from scratch—developing concepts, crafting narratives, and turning creative chaos into content people actually connect with. I’m especially drawn to lifestyle media, pop culture, and formats that blend entertainment with authenticity and impact.

Outside of work, I’m a curious soul who loves long walks by the sea, spontaneous travel plans, people-watching, and finding inspiration in the small, everyday moments (usually followed by a note in my phone that starts with “this could be a show”). I thrive in collaborative spaces, love exchanging perspectives, and believe the best ideas often start with a simple conversation—and maybe a good coffee

people.biography:
Aymen Sarraj is a Growth & Partnerships Architect at Betawaves, operating at the intersection of innovation, digital transformation, and venture capital. He helps entrepreneurs turn their ideas into scalable, investable, and commercially viable businesses. Aymen works directly with founders, diving into the trenches to build programs and create the capital structures that support their growth and success. 

Aymen’s impact extends beyond individual startups to driving ecosystem development. He works to unite operators, investors, and enablers, fostering synergies that create growth-driven ecosystems across Africa. By designing and implementing founder-centric programs, he plays a key role in enhancing regional economies and empowering entrepreneurs. 

As part of Betaventures, the venture capital arm of Betawaves, Aymen contributes to early-stage support and investment initiatives, collaborating closely with founders from day one to shape businesses that are ready for investment and market success. His experience in both venture-building and ecosystem development allows him to translate real-world startup dynamics into scalable venture platforms. 

Aymen is driven by a passion for execution and collaboration, focused on building bridges and creating spaces where ambition meets opportunity and startups can scale with purpose and real impact.

sessions.title: What Kind of Support Does Your Startup Actually Need?

people.biography:
Bill joined QED as a Special Advisor in the fall of 2014 and became a Partner in 2015. He is currently Head of Global Early Stage Investments after six years as Head of International, leading QED’s Investment teams in Latin America, Europe and Asia.

Prior to joining QED, Bill spent nearly 20 years at Capital One, spanning several roles and leading several businesses. He spent the first 6 years of his career leading Marketing, product development and credit policy for Capital One’s subprime credit card business; ultimately having overall P&L responsibility, and growing the business to become the most significant player in the market. He moved on to spend 2 years in various new business development roles, spanning the telecom, medical finance and small business finance industries. Bill spent 3 years as Deputy Chief Credit Officer for the bank, playing nearly every role there was to play in the central credit function, after helping build the department from scratch in 2002. Bill then pivoted his career to general management, leading Capital One’s Canadian, and ultimately International businesses, over the course of 6 years. Profitability of the business grew significantly under Bill’s leadership, through new product and channel introductions, acquisitions, and significant cost take out. During Bill’s last 3 years at Capital One, he led its Co-Brand and Private Label credit card business, building the business nearly from scratch to one of the top few players in the US market, through a series of acquisitions, most notably including leading the acquisition and post-merger integration of HSBC’s US credit card business, which closed in May 2012.

Bill graduated with a BA in economics from the University of Michigan, and competed the SEP program at Stanford GSB.

sessions.title: Are Cross-Border Collaborations Primarily Driven by Capital Flows or by Market Needs?

people.biography:
Ceasar Nyagah is an experienced investment professional with over 16 years in private equity, venture capital, M&A, and technology operations. As Investment Principal at Chui Ventures, he focuses on investing in early-stage African technology startups in the pre-seed and seed stages. 
Throughout his career, Ceasar has played a pivotal role in sourcing, executing, and managing investments across multiple industries, working with both entrepreneurs and institutional investors. His prior roles at Admaius Capital, Partech Partners, and Fanisi Capital have given him deep deal structuring, portfolio management, and fundraising expertise.
A strong advocate for Africa’s innovation ecosystem, Ceasar actively supports startups as an angel investor and advisor, helping founders navigate capital-raising and scale their businesses.
Outside of work, he enjoys spending quality time with family and friends. He has also taken up golf, a sport he enjoys because it has many parallels to life's journey. 
He holds a BSc in Applied Accounting from Oxford Brookes University and an MBA from Strathmore Business School. Ceasar is a chartered accountant (ACCA) and a Global Shaper alumnus of the World Economic Forum.

sessions.title: Is Risk Universal? Rethinking Risks in Emerging Markets

people.biography:
Clara joined AWS in September 2020 and brings over 20 years of IT industry expertise to her role as Global Program Lead for AWS TalentBridge within the AWS Partner Organization, a position she has held since 2023.

In this strategic role, Clara addresses the critical AWS technology skills gap by forging partnerships between AWS's global Partner Network and community-based skilling organizations. Her work focuses on three key areas: building sustainable talent pipelines for next-generation cloud professionals, expanding access to technology careers for underrepresented communities, and creating pathways for career advancement within the AWS network. Through these initiatives, Clara connects AWS Partners and Customers with the skilled workforce they need to drive innovation and growth.

Clara's approach combines strategic program leadership with hands-on collaboration, working across regions to identify skills gaps, develop training pathways, and measure program impact. Her work directly supports AWS's commitment to training millions of people with cloud skills while advancing diversity and inclusion in the technology sector.

Clara holds a BA in English from the University at Albany, State University of New York, and an MBA from Syracuse University, bringing a unique blend of communication expertise and business acumen to workforce development in the cloud computing space.

Outside of work, Clara enjoys spending time with her family – namely her two grandchildren, playing tennis, skiing, sailing, taking long rides on her bicycle, reading, writing, and dreaming.

sessions.title: HUMAN vs. SILICON: The Great Talent Showdown

people.biography:
Dara Ghosheh always had a passion for the kitchen that began early in her childhood. Cookies and
ice-cream played an important role growing up as she would always bake cookies and distribute
them to her neighbors, and every Thursday, a young Dara and her father had a tradition of going out
for ice-cream. So the sweet confection, along with baking, hold a very dear place in her heart.
Originally Palestinian, Dara grew up in Jeddah and summered in Jordan. She graduated in 2005
from the British IG system, and in 2010 she received a bachelor’s degree in Mass Communication
from the American University in Cairo, with a specialization in Integrated Marketing Communica-
tion.
After graduating, Dara had a difficult time finding employment as the Revolution was slowly taking
shape and companies were reluctant to make new hires in marketing. After two years of job search-
es that proved futile, Dara joined the marketing department of a start-up, and soon after was hired
by a corporation to fill a position in its’ CSR department.
Her passion for baking and for ice-cream never subsided throughout the years, and in 2014, Dara
enrolled in a course titled, Gelato-Making Class at Carpigiani University, in Bologne, Italy. After
spending a month of learning the basics of gelato making, Dara was encouraged by her husband to
follow her passion, and so she began studying the concept of creating an ice-cream parlor that was a
destination targeted by customers, and not just a spontaneous purchase.
Dara spent a year and a half developing flavors, testing them, and creating something that combined
the best of gelato and the best of ice-cream together. She then spent the years between 2013 and
2016 testing flavors on a household machine, while she was living between Cairo and Amsterdam.
In May of 2017, Dara had her first child, and in June, she acquired her first professional machine.
That was when she began developing recipes for her own Ice-Cream shop.
The first branch of Dara’s Ice-Cream opened at Galleria 40 in Sheikh Zayed in 2018, the second
opened in 2019 at White by The Waterway in Fifth Settlement, the third is a seasonal branch in the
North Coast, with a current number of 11 branches in Cairo, as many seasonal branches and 3 shops
in KSA. Dara still retains her secret recipes, and combines all the ice-cream flavors herself, she be-
lieves in remaining hands-on because she continues to regard her work not as a job, but as a passion
that she was able to turn into a career.

sessions.title: Building a Collab People Love: From idea to Experience

people.biography:
Because I believe in the untapped potential in each and every one of us, I develop AI products to automate intelligent processes, offering people more space to unfold their greatest potential. With every AI solution I deploy, someone is given the opportunity to step up to their true potential. 

AI is not only my dream job, but the lens in which I learn about the world, people and perspectives. Creating computer programs that can autonomously think and decide fascinates me. Every day I have the privilege of experiencing a priceless combination of art and science, envisioning and implementing, learning and impacting. 

I am a passionate AI & Data Science Expert with a strong business acumen and a solid track record of implementing AI solutions to solve complex business challenges. Over the past 15 years, I have successfully implemented predictive, descriptive and prescriptive analytics delivering value in a wide variety of verticals including sales, marketing, pricing, finance, industry 4.0, drug discovery and cancer biology.

My achievements prove the power of my grit, talent and passion. At Bayer, I initiated and led an AI-innovation project that has been recognised as one of the top three remarkable projects globally in the area of emerging technology. Also, I won the “Distinguished Women in Data Science” global award during my first year. At our startup, we achieved 6 fold growth within 3 years. At StepStone, I have driven and implemented projects with ROI exceeding 5 million euros per year. 
During my academic career, I graduated top of my class with Honors, was awarded a Master's scholarship from the University of Bonn and the state of North Rhine Westphalia, and won the finalist position for Google’s Women In Tech scholarship.

At Bayer, I initiated and led an AI-innovation project that has been recognised as one of the top three remarkable projects globally in the area of emerging technology. Also, I won the “Distinguished Women in Data Science” global award during my first year. At our startup, we achieved 6 fold growth within 3 years. At StepStone, I have driven and implemented projects with ROI exceeding 5 million euros per year. 
During my academic career, I graduated top of my class with Honors, was awarded a Master's scholarship from the University of Bonn and the state of North Rhine Westphalia, and won the finalist position for Google’s Women In Tech scholarship.

people.biography:
Dina El-Mofty is a community builder, thought leader, and angel investor dedicated to empowering entrepreneurs and advancing the wellness movement across the region. Recognized by Arabian Business as one of the World’s Most Influential Young Arabs Under 40, Dina is the Founder and Chair of INJAZ Egypt, a leading organization driving entrepreneurial education and youth empowerment nationwide. She is also the Co-Founder of, Egypt’s largest celebration of health and wellness, bringing together world-class experts and holistic experiences that inspire people to live more consciously and fully. She is also a partner at Escape Code one of Egypt’s leading luxury travel companies, renowned for curating insider-led journeys and extraordinary, rarely accessible experiences across the country. 

A familiar face on Egyptian television, Dina served as a judge on Egypt’s first entrepreneurial program—aired on CBC as Hona Al Shabab and later Al Forsa—where she championed emerging startups and showcased Egypt’s most promising young entrepreneurs.

Under her leadership, INJAZ Egypt has impacted over one million young people, equipping them with entrepreneurial, financial literacy, and work-readiness skills. Through its pioneering startup incubator, the organization has launched, accelerated, and seed-funded nearly one hundred successful ventures, facilitating annual startup exchanges with Silicon Valley to bridge global innovation ecosystems.

Dina’s impact and leadership have earned her multiple accolades, including the Arabian Business Young Achiever Award and recognition among the Top 50 Women in Business in Egypt. She holds a graduate degree from the prestigious Fletcher School at Tufts University.

Beyond entrepreneurship, Dina is a passionate advocate for personal growth and holistic well-being. Having trained with world-renowned thought leaders in human potential and wellness, she integrates over two decades of experience to mentor CEOs, founders, and professionals seeking to elevate their performance and align with their purpose. Through her coaching, mentorship programs, and transformational retreats, she helps people unlock inner clarity, balance ambition with well-being, and create meaningful success in all areas of life.

A proud Spelman College alumna, she also studied the Management of Technology at New York University and completed executive programs in AI and Ethics at MIT Sloan and Harvard University. When she's not shaping the future of AI, she’s shaping future leaders—starting with her two sons and extending to the many mentees she inspires to color outside the lines, defy the odds, and reimagine what’s possible.

people.biography:
Dotun Olowoporoku is the Managing Partner at Ventures Platform, a Pan-African early-stage VC fund that invests in innovative startups with differentiated and defensible market-creating innovations. Before his role at Ventures Platform, Dotun served as the Chief Commercial Officer at Moniepoint, a series C fintech startup that facilitates financial services for the next billion Africans through payment and banking services to over 500,000 businesses. overseeing the company’s ecosystem engagement, investor relationships, corporate development, M&A, and strategic expansion. Prior to that, he was a Principal at Novastar Ventures, a pan-African early-stage VC firm where he led post-series A investments.
Dotun's career began in academia as a Post-doctoral Research Fellow on air quality and climate change in Bristol, England. This research background provides him with a unique analytical perspective in his investment roles. In 2012, he took an entrepreneurial path and founded an on-demand food delivery platform. The platform saw significant growth under his leadership, scaling across three cities in the UK, and forming a strategic partnership with Just-Eat UK Plc in 2015.
He hosts the Building the Future podcast, where he engages in thought-provoking discussions about Africa's growth narrative. His influence expands to several African startups where he serves as an angel investor and board member, contributing to their strategic direction and growth.

sessions.title: Why Global Investors are Looking at Africa?

people.biography:
Emon Shakoor is a Saudi neuroscience researcher turned venture capitalist and entrepreneur, widely recognized for her pioneering work at the intersection of innovation, inclusion, and investment. She is the Founder & CEO of Blossom Accelerator — one of the region’s most influential innovation and investment infrastructure platforms, building systems that power emerging technology, capital flows, and global market entry into Saudi Arabia.

Under her leadership, Blossom designs and operates large-scale accelerators, corporate innovation programs, venture partnerships, and FDI soft-landing pipelines. Through its internationally recognized SoftLanding Program, Blossom attracts high-growth startups from around the world to enter, set up, and scale in Saudi Arabia — enabling frictionless market access, regulatory support, and successful go-to-market pathways. Blossom has become a central gateway for global founders contributing to the Kingdom’s rapidly expanding innovation economy.

A trusted partner to both government and industry, Emon has led innovation and investment programs with national entities including the Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (MCIT), NVIDIA, NEOM, Diriyah, TikTok, Savola, and others — as well as FDI-focused soft-landing partnerships with the Ministry of Investment (MISA). Through these partnerships, she has bridged global technologies with Saudi corporates, investors, and giga-projects, accelerating the Kingdom’s position as a global hub for innovation.

Emon also serves as a Venture Partner at Oryx Fund and is an active angel investor, advisor, and member of the opportunity committee at Oqal, the GCC’s largest angel investment network. Her work has been recognized by the World Economic Forum, Stanford University, Forbes, Bloomberg, and numerous global institutions for its impact on technology ecosystems and inclusive economic growth.

Before entering venture capital, she earned a Bachelor’s in Cognitive Science from UC San Diego, conducting research on mirror neurons and social cognition, and later led clinical drug trials for Pfizer at PAREXEL.

A distinguished Global Shaper who represented the 30 Under 30 cohort at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Emon is also a sought-after TEDx and global keynote speaker. Featured on the covers of Entrepreneur Middle East and Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, she is regarded as one of the Middle East’s most dynamic leaders shaping the future of technology, investment, and economic transformation.

people.biography:
I am a family man at heart, I believe that Business wasn't something that I picked, it picked me. I grew up with a pair of entrepreneurial. Losing my father at a young age, emersed me in the realities of building, running, and sustaining a business early on in my life. This made me understand that once you own a business you don't only carry a company, but a legacy.

But I always had a passion for finance, and I chased this passion with global banks. My experience in banking sparked my drive and shaped who I am today. 

My time in banking sharpened my perspective and helped define who I am professionally today. It also revealed a clear gap in the market—elite opportunities were often reserved for a select few, leaving many capable and ambitious individuals without access.

This created my aim which is to bridge that gap by offering private-banking-style business and investment opportunities to those who typically cannot access them, but who seek unique opportunities to grow their wealth and generate strong returns. Everything I build is rooted in exclusivity, trust, and long-term value creation.

Outside of business, I enjoy shooting, traveling and staying connected to pop culture, which helps me stay grounded, curious, and balanced.

people.biography:
Estelle Koné is an impact investor on a mission to accelerate sustainable growth for African SMEs. She is a General Partner at Sabou Capital, which invests in high-impact businesses across West and Central Africa.
Estelle began her career at Goldman Sachs in New York, where she spent a decade designing data-driven investment and risk strategies across trading, investment banking, and private equity. She holds a PhD in Industrial Engineering and is currently pursuing her MBA at The Wharton School.
Originally from Burkina Faso and shaped by decades across Europe and North America, Estelle brings a global perspective and a systems-thinking approach to designing practical solutions for entrepreneurs and investors alike. Her work blends finance, data analytics, and technology to unlock scalable impact.
Beyond her work in investment strategy and data-driven innovation, Estelle is energized by movement and discovery. She is a salsa dancer, an amateur photographer chasing sunsets around the world, and a passionate traveler always eager to explore new cultures.

people.biography:
Fabio Lorenzon is a 28-year old entrepreneur working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, operations, and real-world business execution.
He is the Founder & CEO of SolutioAI, an AI consulting company that helps organizations build practical, long-term AI solutions by starting from how businesses actually work and not from buzzwords or generic tools.
At SolutioAI, Fabio collaborates with manufacturing companies, supply chains, legal firms, and fast-growing organizations across Europe and the MENA region, designing custom AI systems that improve efficiency, decision-making, and scalability. His work spans areas such as computer vision, predictive analytics, and generative AI, always with a strong focus on process design, governance, and real operational impact. A key principle of his approach is that intellectual property remains with the client, making AI a true business asset rather than a dependency.
Alongside SolutioAI, Fabio is also Managing Partner of Lorenzon, a precision-mechanical manufacturing company serving the steel and heavy industry sectors. He grew up inside the business, working across production, quality, purchasing, and sales, before taking on the leadership role. This hands-on industrial background strongly shapes the way he thinks about technology: pragmatic, measurable, and grounded in execution.
Fabio holds both a BSc and MSc in Industrial Engineering from Politecnico di Milano and completed the Artificial Intelligence for Executives program at IESE Business School.
Earlier in his career, he worked as delivery operations manager for Amazon Italy, strengthening his exposure to large scale processes and data driven decision making.
Today, Fabio speaks about AI as an entrepreneur first, and a technologist second, convinced that AI creates real value only when it serves people, processes, and clear business goals, and when entrepreneurs learn to think beyond single ventures to build systems that last.

people.biography:
I am Habeeba Hamed, the Marketing Manager at Dash Management, with over six years of experience contributing to the growth and evolution of a full-service marketing agency.

My journey into marketing began with a genuine fascination for its power,the ability of a strong strategy or campaign to completely shift a brand’s direction and create meaningful impact. This passion led me to study marketing and later join Dash at a very early stage, when the agency consisted of only three people. I started as a Junior Account Manager, but in practice, I took on multiple responsibilities across the business, from pitching to clients and managing accounts to supporting operations and finances. Although this phase was demanding and at times overwhelming, it became the most formative period of my career. It gave me a deep understanding of the full marketing and agency process, taught me what to expect and what to avoid, and most importantly, encouraged me to think bigger and dream without limits.

I do not see Dash as just an agency I work with,it is a place I deeply belong to. I take pride in witnessing its transformation from a small team with no formal structure into an organization of nearly 50 employees, operating across six specialized departments, and further expanding with the launch of our sister company, DPH, our production house.

Throughout my journey, I learned how to lead by experience, often being the first to explore new paths and build processes from the ground up. While this approach can be a double-edged sword, it helped me develop my own management style rooted in adaptability, accountability, and continuous learning. I strongly believe in evolving with the market and refining my leadership approach as the industry changes.

My goal is to continue growing Dash, creating meaningful impact for our clients, and fostering a positive, ethical, and inspiring environment for my team because I believe integrity, even when it slows progress, always leads to lasting success.

people.biography:
Hadi Halabi is the Founder and CEO of Stryde, the first regulated sports investment platform empowering individuals and institutions to seamlessly invest in global sports. Prior to founding Stryde, Hadi built his career in investment banking, advising on major deals across Europe and the Middle East. But behind the spreadsheets, he always had an obsession with the worlds of sports, tech and capital. Luckily Stryde combines all of the above.

Stryde was born from two simple observations: Nothing beats the passion for sports and sports has significantly outperformed the market as an asset class, yet almost no one gets the chance to invest. Hadi decided to change that, and today Stryde has grown into a fast-moving platform serving thousands of investors and partnering with sports clubs, leagues, and entertainment IP globally.

Hadi is a big sports fan who enjoys watching most sports, a passionate supporter of Manchester United and enjoys playing lots of padel.

sessions.title: Where Real Value Is Being Built in Sports

people.biography:
Hannah Attalah is the founder and Creative Director of Oceanus, a London-based luxury fashion house recognised for its signature beaded dresses, embellished swimwear, and statement resortwear. Half Irish and half Lebanese, Hannah was born and raised in London — a multicultural upbringing that continues to shape Oceanus’s global perspective, aesthetic depth, and storytelling.

Hannah was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30, recognising her as one of Europe’s most influential young entrepreneurs for redefining contemporary luxury through a founder-led, design-driven business. Since launching the brand, she has built Oceanus into an internationally stocked label celebrated for its intricate hand-beading, sculptural silhouettes, and emotionally resonant design language inspired by mythology, travel, and the natural world.

Oceanus is stocked by leading luxury retailers and resort destinations across the UK, Europe, the Middle East, and the US, with key partners including Harvey Nichols, Selfridges, Printemps, Anthropologie, and Revolve, alongside a growing network of premium concept stores and five-star hotel boutiques. The brand has also developed strong direct-to-consumer traction, supported by a highly engaged global customer base and strong sell-through across hero categories.

Beyond creative direction, Hannah leads brand strategy, product architecture, and international expansion, combining artistic vision with commercial discipline. Her founder-led approach positions Oceanus not only as a fashion brand, but as a scalable global luxury business rooted in craftsmanship, cultural nuance, and long-term brand equity.

sessions.title: What it Takes to Build an Iconic Brand

Hasan Haider has over 15 years of experience investing in MENA startups. Hasan is the Founder and Managing Partner of +VC, the most active early stage venture capital firm in the MENA region. Hasan was previously Managing Partner, MENA at 500 Startups and led the firms growth in the MENA Region. Hasan has invested in over 280 startups in the region over the course of the last 5 years, including seed investments in companies like Calo, Floward, Eyewa, Thndr and Holo.
Prior to 500, Hasan was the co-founder and CEO of Tenmou, the first business angel’s organization in Bahrain and one of the first in the MENA region. Hasan’s work in developing angel investment has been picked up as a case study by the World Bank and Babson College. Previously, Hasan’s career was in finance and investment banking at Sico where he spent a number of years.

people.biography:
I am a content strategist and entrepreneur, and the founder of Homus, a fast-growing media brand focused on making business, money, and strategy accessible to a wider audience. My work sits at the intersection of content, storytelling, and revenue, helping founders and brands turn attention into real business outcomes rather than vanity metrics.

Over the past few years, I have built and advised multiple ventures across media, food, transportation, and consulting, with a strong focus on short-form content as a growth engine. I am particularly interested in how founders can use content as leverage, not just for visibility, but for sales, partnerships, and long-term brand equity.

My approach is practical and data-driven, grounded in real execution rather than theory. I believe content should serve a clear purpose, reflect a strong vision, and ultimately move the business forward. When I am not building or advising, I spend my time breaking down complex ideas into simple frameworks and helping founders communicate what they do in a way that is clear, compelling, and commercially effective.

people.biography:
Ihsan Anabtawi is a senior technology and business executive with over two decades of experience building and leading large-scale cloud, AI, and digital platform businesses across the Middle East, Africa, and emerging markets. 

Most recently, he served as Managing Director and Regional Head for AI & Cloud Solutions at Amazon Web Services (AWS) for the MENAT region. In this role, he led specialist sales, strategy, go-to-market, and solutions architecture, while spearheading national generative AI initiatives.

Prior to AWS, Ihsan was a founding executive and the Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer of Core42 (G42 Group). He designed and led the commercial organization for the multi-billion-dollar enterprise AI and cloud platform, overseeing more than 1,100 employees and leading national-scale enterprise AI programs.

Ihsan’s career includes nearly 20 years at Microsoft in various senior leadership positions. As Chief Operating and Marketing Officer and Chief Commercial Officer for Microsoft UAE, he led one of the company’s most strategic global markets, scaling the business to exceed $1 billion in annual revenue and launching the region’s first cloud data centers. He also served as COO for Microsoft’s largest Gulf cluster and led the Cloud & Enterprise division across 15+ emerging markets.

An active entrepreneur and investor, Ihsan founded an Enterprise AI company in stealth mode and regularly serves as an advisor to global private equity firms, global consulting firms, and venture capital funds on AI investment, expansion strategy, and regional go-to-market models. He also mentors and advises a portfolio of early-stage and growth-stage technology companies. 

He holds a B.Sc. in Computer Science from the University of Jordan and is an alumnus of executive programs at The Wharton School, INSEAD, and the Kellogg School of Management.

people.biography:
Imèn Meliane is a global leader with over 20 years of experience advancing conservation, climate adaptation, and sustainable development. Born in Tunisia, she has worked across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas, bridging local realities with international policy and finance.
She has advised governments, multilateral institutions, and foundations in more than 70 countries, shaping strategies on marine conservation, nature-based solutions, climate resilience, and access to climate finance. She currently is a Senior Advisor to the Africa Adaptation Initiative (AAI), supporting high-level efforts to scale adaptation action and mobilize finance for Africa’s most climate-vulnerable countries.
Imèn has held senior roles with the Adaptation Fund, UNDP, The Nature Conservancy, and IUCN. She is currently Councillor and Vice President of IUCN, contributing to global environmental governance and strategic reform. She has also been Vice Chair of the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas and worked extensively across major multilateral processes, including the UNFCCC and the Convention on Biological Diversity.
She holds advanced degrees in marine environmental management from Tunisia and Spain, and is fluent in Arabic, English, French, and Spanish.

people.biography: Ismael Faro is the Vice President of Quantum + AI at IBM Research, and he holds the recognition of Distinguished Engineer for his technical contributions. Notably, he was principal architect for first public Quantum Cloud platform, the IBM Quantum Experience, back in 2016. Faro is also recognized as one of the pioneering contributors to the open-source quantum computing software development framework Qiskit. Currently, his responsibilities include spearheading the development of Quantum + AI software and services integrate novel research, focus on leveraging AI to optimize key parts of the quantum software stack and a research agentic open source stack. Beyond his executive roles, Ismael has a history of collaboration with research, developer, and entrepreneurial communities, actively engaging in open-source projects. As an entrepreneur, he has co-founded several startups that leverage cutting-edge technologies such as edge computing, distributed computing, AI, and prioritize enhancing user experiences through technological innovation.

sessions.title: Building Bridges: How AI and Quantum Computing Converge
sessions.description:
Startups are entering a new era where the fusion of AI and quantum computing will define the next generation of breakthrough technologies and products, and IBM is uniquely positioned to help them lead that transformation. IBM’s vision is clear: by combining quantum‑centric supercomputing with advanced AI capabilities, we aim to empower innovators to solve problems once thought impossible. The future are hybrid architectures, integrating CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, and QPUs into a unified computational fabric. 

IBM Quantum is eliminating barriers that have historically slowed quantum development, thanks lead project as the Open Source frameworks Qiskit, cloud‑accessible QPUs, quantum cloud functions and enterprise‑grade AI platforms. These capabilities allow small teams to move with the speed and precision, compressing the path from concept to prototype in research space to create the future quantum+AI products. Thanks to that, and new startup ecosystem is emerging partnership with industry leaders in materials, health, energy, and finance, IBM provides startups with a launchpad to develop, validate, and scale quantum‑enhanced applications. From quantum chemistry simulation to optimization and next‑generation solvers, startups gain both the tools and the partnership needed to explore new computational frontiers.

IBM’s vision is to be the bridge that helps founders turn quantum potential into real‑world products. By converging AI and quantum in a developer‑friendly, scalable, and open ecosystem, we enable the next wave of bold innovators to create solutions that reshape industries and define the coming decade of deep‑tech entrepreneurship.

Javier has extensive experience in technology and telecom ventures, being advisor and serving on the boards of multiple companies as well as combining his professional work with his passion for motorsports as a member of the McLaren Racing Advisory Board.

people.biography:
Hailing from the small town of Prescott, Jeremy graduated from the University of Arizona and promptly moved to Los Angeles to pursue his entertainment industry dream. After working as a writer and producer on several animated shows, Jeremy rose to notoriety with his high concept ideas and intense love of action and comedy. This enthusiasm spilled over, as he, along with co-writer Jim Krieg wrote the much-lauded Scooby-Doo / Supernatural crossover that is still considered one of the best episodes of this long-running CW series. “Scoobynatural” premiered to thousands of fans at the Kodak Theatre during PaleyFest to huge acclaim. 
 
The crossover was so successful, that the producers of Supernatural asked Adams to write for the 15th and final season of the beloved show. Jeremy joined the writing staff as a story editor, where he penned two solo episodes. He became a "fan favorite" for his fast-paced and humorous scripts, gaining him the hashtag #nicestguyinhollywood within the online Supernatural community. 
 
After writing several very successful films for LEGO and DC, LEGO also asked Jeremy to produce, write, and story edit their new original show called "Monkie Kid." The cultural partnership took Adams to China to develop the show and participate in a documentary about its making with their international partners.
 
Abroad, Monkie Kid has been a massive success, with the first "special" reaching over fifty million viewers within the first week of release. 
 
Adams quickly began to apply his craft to the delight of adult animation fans, writing the critically acclaimed Mortal Kombat Legends: Scorpion’s Revenge, and working closely with artist and legend Bruce Timm, to write the pulpy 70’s style flick Batman: Soul of the Dragon. Though his free time is limited, Adams has carved out another career in comic books, writing characters such as The Flash, Green Lantern, Flash Gordon and the current Aquaman book.
 
With many more movies, tv, and comics on the horizon, Jeremy is always writing and creating new projects, all of which possess unbeatable action and plenty of heart.

Prior to his current role, Kareem held progressive leadership positions including MEA AI & Analytics Regional Manager at Ericsson, Data Science & Analytics Manager at Grey Skies, and Telecom Engineering Technical Lead at Vodafone. He has also contributed to academia as a part-time Research Associate at the American University in Cairo (AUC), focusing on AI applications in telecommunications networks.

Karim Hussein is Managing Partner at Algebra Ventures. He is a technology veteran with deep experience in product and innovation management and rapid business growth and scaling – particularly in the healthcare and financial services markets. 

Karim has been an active investor and mentor to a number of technology businesses in Egypt and the US. He is founder and Chairman of D-Kimia Diagnostic Solutions developing fast, affordable, and accurate medical diagnostics using nano-technology and focused on controlling the Hepatitis C epidemic in Egypt and globally. 

Karim has served on the board of D-Kimia, Integreight, Shezlong.com, Prognos.ai, and Simplex Arabia CNC Solutions. He is also Chairman of the entrepreneurship committee of the Egyptian National Competitiveness Council, a mentor to high impact entrepreneurs through the Endeavor network, and a fellow of the Aspen Global Leadership Network.

Previously, Karim was SVP, Products and Engineering at WebMD, Inc., directing product management, technology strategy and engineering. Prior to WebMD, Karim was co-founder and CTO of Riskclick, Inc., a software firm specializing in commercial insurance applications. He also was a senior associate at Booz Allen & Hamilton where he was a member of the Global e-Commerce team.

people.biography:
Karim Tadjeddine is the Founder of Qantara Tech Fund (QATEF). QATEF is set to become the first tech cross-fertilization investment platform between GCC and Europe. GCC has prioritized technological transformation and the attraction of tech talent. QATEF offers a tangible solution to accelerate this ambition by investing and facilitating the localization of technologies and European tech talent in GCC. 
Since 2022, Karim Tadjeddine has Co-Founded Partech Impact Fund. Partech is a global tech investment firm, managing 3Bn€ of assets, with a portfolio > 400 startups. Partech Impact invests specifically in Impact-native x Tech startups, at Growth stage. Partech Impact has raised >250M€ and has invested to date more than 70M€ in 5 investments.
From 2006 to 2022, Karim was one of the world-wide leaders of McKinsey. He was Global Leader of Economic and Social Development Domain. He supported Governments, Corporates, Financial Institutions and Investment Funds, across more than 20 countries.
From 2001 to 2006, Karim worked in Ministry of Finance in France. He was in charge of improving SME financing, launching first government backed VC funds. He also supported the creation of the Government Shareholding Agency, managing 180 Bn€ of government owned assets, in Industry and Service.
Karim has invested as Business Angel, since 2016, in more than 25 start-ups, with a focus on environmental transition, education and health. 
Karim has strong personal engagements to promote economic empowerment. He is Chairman of Generation France and Vice-Chairman of Positiv. Generation has supported more than 100 000 learners worldwide into getting a job. Positiv has supported more than 25 000 entrepreneurs from left-behind neighborhoods.
Karim has regularly participated in expert panels, including Tech for Good Summit and the G7 High Level Advisory Group. Karim has published articles on development and tech, such as, “Inequality: A persisting challenge and its implications”.

people.biography:
Karima El Hakim is the Partner for Africa at Plug and Play Tech Center, where she leads the firm’s venture activities on the continent and oversees the expansion of its open innovation and corporate innovation activities across African markets. Her work focuses on fintech, artificial intelligence, smart cities, and industrial innovation, with a strong emphasis on building scalable, market-driven innovation ecosystems.

Karima is an MIT Foundry Fellow, Co-Chair for Africa at the MENA Fintech Association, and Co-Chair of the Innovation and Entrepreneurship Committee at the American Chamber of Commerce in Egypt. She is also a board member of a financial services company and previously served on the Economic Development Committee of the National Council for Women for the 2025 term.

Prior to her current role, Karima held senior leadership positions in venture investing and ecosystem development in Falak Startups and Fawry. Her mission is to scale impactful, inclusive innovation across African markets while strengthening the link between policy, capital, and technology.

people.biography:
Kim Fox is a leading voice in podcasting and audio storytelling, blending expertise in media education, production and business strategy. As a Professor of Practice at The American University in Cairo (AUC), she specializes in radio, audio and podcasting, with a focus on Global Majority creators.
With decades of experience in the U.S. radio industry and a deep understanding of emerging audio trends, Kim doesn’t just teach podcasting, she produces, researches and innovates in the space. She is the founder of PodFest Cairo, the first podcasting conference in Egypt and Africa, bringing together creators, brands and thought leaders to explore the power of audio in business and media.
Kim is also the executive producer of the multi-award-winning bilingual podcast, Ehky Ya Masr (Tell Your Story, Egypt), a narrative nonfiction podcast that elevates underrepresented voices in the region. Her collaborative audio piece Birdland Refracted, co-produced with Emiliano Quintanar (Milio Boogie), was shortlisted for the Audio Flux Circuit 05 competition and selected as one of four Circuit Selects. It premiered at the Smithsonian's Hirshhorn Museum during the Sound Scene Festival last year.
As an entrepreneur at heart, Kim helps businesses, startups and independent creators understand how to leverage podcasting as a brand asset, whether for customer engagement, thought leadership or monetization. She has conducted global workshops and training sessions in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and more, helping professionals and businesses develop impactful audio strategies without the need for expensive setups or complex production.
Her academic research focuses on Global Majority podcasters, decolonizing podcast studies and the intersection of audio and AI, ensuring that new voices and perspectives are represented in the global podcasting ecosystem. She has coached her students to produce over 150 award-winning audio projects, many of which have gained international recognition.
Beyond academia, Kim recently served as Co-President of the Association for Independents in Radio (AIR) and is the past President of the Broadcast Education Association (BEA). She continues to shape the future of podcasting through her work as a researcher, producer and advocate for inclusive storytelling.
For entrepreneurs looking to harness the power of audio, build a podcasting brand, or explore innovative audio-first marketing strategies, Kim Fox is the go-to expert.

people.biography:
Kola is an experienced investor, insightful non-executive director, and company chair who is passionate about supporting the growth of startups. He is the Founding Partner at the Pan-African early-stage VC fund, Ventures Platform Fund.

He has a proven track record of success with investments in over 100 companies across Africa, India, and the US. This includes payment companies like Paystack and healthcare companies like MDaaS. Kola was also the founder and former CEO of Emerging Platforms, a leading enterprise software provider in West Africa. He has established extensive networks in the private sector, development partners, financiers, governments, and regulators.

With vast experience in Africa's most significant economic market, Kola is an entrepreneur, technology operator, and venture capital investor. He brings expertise across various sectors, including venture capital, technology, media, agriculture, infrastructure, publishing, and real estate. Additionally, he has a strong interest in the arts.

Kola actively participates in mentoring programs such as XL Africa, the World Bank Accelerator, and Google Launchpad Accelerator. He serves on the boards of multiple organizations, including ARM Financial Advisers and Iron Global Markets. Until recently, he served as Chairman of the board of governors for the Lagos Angel Network. He was also appointed to the board of Enhancing Financial Innovation & Access Limited by Guarantee (EFInA) and the Lagos State Research and Innovation Council (LASRIC**)**

As an avid art patron, Kola is a member of the advisory board of the Yemisi Shyllon Art Museum and the Africa Acquisitions Committee (AAC) at the Tate Museum. He is also a member of the Young Presidents' Organization (YPO) and a fellow of the Aspen Institute USA (ALIWA) and the African Leadership Institute (Tutu Fellowship).

Kola holds a degree in Electrical Engineering and a Master's in Business Administration with a specialization in Finance. He has furthered his education at prestigious institutions such as Berkeley, Harvard, and the Lagos Business School.

With a passion for mentoring and advising young entrepreneurs who are creating solutions for underserved markets, Kola has been invited to speak at numerous local and international events on topics like technology, entrepreneurship, social change, and more. Notably, he gave a [TED talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UFrRm7G1CQk) at TEDxEuston on the topic "Who will own our future unicorns?" and spoke at Techcrunch Startup Battlefield Africa 2019.

Kola has received multiple awards and has been featured in various lists, recognizing his contributions to the African tech industry and beyond.

In his free time, he enjoys writing on his blog and Twitter about topics he is passionate about, reading books, and spending time with his family.

speaker.biography:
Kola is an experienced investor, insightful non-executive director, and company chair who is passionate about supporting the growth of startups. He is the Founding Partner at the Pan-African early-stage VC fund, Ventures Platform Fund.

He has a proven track record of success with investments in over 100 companies across Africa, India, and the US. This includes payment companies like Paystack and healthcare companies like MDaaS. Kola was also the founder and former CEO of Emerging Platforms, a leading enterprise software provider in West Africa. He has established extensive networks in the private sector, development partners, financiers, governments, and regulators.

With vast experience in Africa's most significant economic market, Kola is an entrepreneur, technology operator, and venture capital investor. He brings expertise across various sectors, including venture capital, technology, media, agriculture, infrastructure, publishing, and real estate. Additionally, he has a strong interest in the arts.

Kola actively participates in mentoring programs such as XL Africa, the World Bank Accelerator, and Google Launchpad Accelerator. He serves on the boards of multiple organizations, including ARM Financial Advisers and Iron Global Markets. Until recently, he served as Chairman of the board of governors for the Lagos Angel Network. He was also appointed to the board of Enhancing Financial Innovation & Access Limited by Guarantee (EFInA) and the Lagos State Research and Innovation Council (LASRIC**)**

As an avid art patron, Kola is a member of the advisory board of the Yemisi Shyllon Art Museum and the Africa Acquisitions Committee (AAC) at the Tate Museum. He is also a member of the Young Presidents' Organization (YPO) and a fellow of the Aspen Institute USA (ALIWA) and the African Leadership Institute (Tutu Fellowship).

Kola holds a degree in Electrical Engineering and a Master's in Business Administration with a specialization in Finance. He has furthered his education at prestigious institutions such as Berkeley, Harvard, and the Lagos Business School.

With a passion for mentoring and advising young entrepreneurs who are creating solutions for underserved markets, Kola has been invited to speak at numerous local and international events on topics like technology, entrepreneurship, social change, and more. Notably, he gave a [TED talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UFrRm7G1CQk) at TEDxEuston on the topic "Who will own our future unicorns?" and spoke at Techcrunch Startup Battlefield Africa 2019.

Kola has received multiple awards and has been featured in various lists, recognizing his contributions to the African tech industry and beyond.

In his free time, he enjoys writing on his blog and Twitter about topics he is passionate about, reading books, and spending time with his family.

people.biography:
Lenah Hassaballah is a journalist, presenter, and creator best known as the host of Kalam Business, one of the region’s fastest-growing business talk shows, which has garnered 80+ million views in just a few months. With a signature style that blends candid human storytelling, sharp economic insight, and bold, fearless questions, Lenah has redefined how business conversations are told in the Arab world.

Lenah began her media career in politics in 2011, working across some of the region’s most influential news networks, including Al Jazeera and Al Arabiya, where she built a reputation for her on-the-ground reporting.

Today, through Kalam Business on CNN Business Arabic, she sits down with leading entrepreneurs, cultural figures, CEOs, and global thinkers, unpacking their journeys, failures, turning points, and the real stories behind their success. Her work bridges business and humanity, offering audiences a rare mix of impact, insight, and authenticity.

people.biography:
Dr. Maged Ghoneima is an angel investor, professor, and key architect of the Egyptian entrepreneurship ecosystem. As the Founder and General Partner of M Empire Angels, he leverages a unique background in advanced engineering and policy-making to identify and scale high-potential startups.

His technical foundation was built at Northwestern University (PhD, 2006) and through tenure at industry giants Intel and NVIDIA. Returning to academia as a Professor of Mechatronics at Ain Shams University, Maged transitioned from circuit design to ecosystem design. He established the ASU Innovation Hub (iHub) and launched the Innovators Support Fund (ISF) for the Ministry of Higher Education, driving innovation strategy across 98 universities nationwide.

Today, Maged is a founding member of Startup Egypt (Egypt’s leading Entrepreneurship Support NGO) and an active angel investor. His portfolio spans diverse sectors globally, backing over 190 startups that are reshaping industries in more than 30 countries.

sessions.title: The Funding Blind Spot: Are Deeptech Startups Overlooked?

people.biography:
Mahmoud Gomaa is an AI and business ecosystem leader with over 20 years of experience across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific, focused on turning advanced technology into scalable, real-world impact. His work centers on AI adoption at scale, Frugal AI, ecosystem-led growth, and innovation in complex and regulated markets.

He has led business development and market expansion initiatives across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia Pacific for global technology companies including Microsoft, SAP, and Adobe, working closely with enterprises, governments, and partners to move AI and digital platforms from pilots to production.

Across his career, Mahmoud has built and governed multi-party ecosystems involving hyperscalers, systems integrators, telcos, and startups, with a strong focus on Frugal AI models, AI economics, governance, and sustainable scale. As a speaker and moderator, he brings a grounded, execution-driven perspective on GenAI at scale, Frugal AI, AI inclusion, and emerging-market innovation, consistently bridging technology ambition with business and policy realities.

people.biography:
Malak runs A&T Media, which she founded in 2021. A&T Media is a company concentrating on content creation for podcasts, with What I Did Next as its award-winning flagship show. The company is focused on generating English-language content that is from and for the Middle East. What I Did Next can be found on all podcast platforms and on YouTube.

Malak is a communications specialist who has worked across a wide spectrum of the industry. Starting in journalism in the mid-1990’s in New York, Cairo and London, Malak worked for both national newspapers as well as glossy magazines. She worked for Condé Nast publications, Punch Magazine, The Daily Mail newspaper and the Ahram Hebdo newspaper. 

In the early 2000’s she moved into media consultancy and public relations. In London Malak was with Magid, advising banks on investments in the nascent Internet industry. Upon moving to Cairo in 2001, Malak joined Weber Shandwick / Promoseven PR.

Outside the media world, Malak is a member of the Board of Directors of Arab Investments for Urbanization, the owner company of the Semiramis Intercontinental hotel in Cairo, Egypt. 

Malak Fouad received a B.A. (with Hons) in International Relations with French from the University of Kent at Canterbury in the United Kingdom in 1995 and an M.A. in Global Affairs from the American University in Cairo (AUC) in Egypt in 2020. 

Malak speaks English, French and Arabic.

people.biography:
Margreet Magdy is a cross-sector strategist and ecosystem builder with over 15 years of experience across the MENA and Euro-Med regions, working at the intersection of entrepreneurship, inclusive innovation, gender equity, and digital transformation.

She collaborates with founders, accelerators, development organizations, corporates, and public sector partners to design programs and platforms that turn ideas into scalable, real-world impact, with a strong focus on empowering women and youth to access economic opportunities and build sustainable ventures.

Margreet is the founder of You Are س, a holistic initiative advancing women’s professional and economic empowerment across the region, and a founding board member of the Youth Entrepreneurs Network (YEN), where she supports youth-led innovation and ecosystem development.

Known for her systems-thinking approach, Margreet blends strategy, policy insight, and hands-on execution to build connected, future-ready ecosystems that serve both people and institutions. Her work spans mentorship programs, AI-driven training initiatives, digital learning platforms, and multi-stakeholder collaborations.

Whether designing national programs, advising ecosystem players, or curating impactful learning experiences, Margreet brings clarity, purpose, and practical solutions to every space she engages in.

people.biography:
Marriam Mossalli is an entrepreneur, investor, and advisor working at the intersection of culture, capital, and women’s economic participation. For over 15 years, her work has focused on building businesses and platforms that unlock growth in emerging markets while ensuring women are positioned as founders, decision-makers, and investors - not merely beneficiaries. 

In 2011, she founded a luxury and cultural consultancy designed to bridge global brands with the GCC through market entry, brand strategy, and commercialization. What began as advisory work evolved into a launchpad for scalable ventures, public-private collaborations, and founder support across retail, tourism, media, and lifestyle sectors. Embedding female leadership and local talent into business models has remained a core principle of her entrepreneurial and investment approach. 

Alongside consultancy, she actively invests in and co-builds founder-led ventures. She is the co-founder and Chief Marketing Officer of the region’s first clean beauty e-commerce platform, which successfully closed its seed round in 2024 with participation from leading regional investors. She also serves as an investor and executive board advisor to a functional non-alcoholic wellness brand focused on mental well-being, and continues to support early-stage companies operating at the intersection of health, lifestyle, and sustainability. 

Her approach to investment extends beyond capital. She works closely with founders on market positioning, go-to-market strategy, and investor readiness, with a strong focus on scalable and long-term value creation. She has also launched an advisory platform designed to guide female-led startups through critical stages of market entry and capital raising.

Beyond business, she leverages storytelling and access as tools for economic empowerment. She founded a women-focused cultural platform that evolved into an education-funding initiative and actively mentors female founders through regional empowerment programs.

At RiseUp, she brings a founder-investor perspective grounded in execution - focused on how women can build investable businesses, access capital, and scale with purpose in emerging markets.
