people.biography:
Marwa Benhalim is a Libyan-Egyptian artist, curator, and researcher based in Cairo. Her practice examines power structures across intimate and systemic scales, employing research-led and collaborative methodologies to interrogate how social, political, and cultural forces are formed, maintained, and contested.
She is the co-founder and co-director of the Cairo Art Book Fair, a leading regional platform for independent publishing and artistic knowledge production. She is also the director of Switchboard, a curatorial studio that develops experimental, context-responsive curatorial projects, consultancy, and cultural strategy. Switchboard houses the Sekoun Art Residency Program and facilitates ongoing public programs, including monthly gatherings dedicated to critical dialogue and exchange.
Benhalim is the founder and lead editor of Ta3amana Publishing, a research-based publishing initiative that engages food and culinary systems as critical entry points into questions of cultural production, gender, labor, and alternative socio-political practices.
In 2024, she curated Does a River Shape a Table? at the Grand Egyptian Museum, an exhibition examining the historical and contemporary conditions of agricultural practices in Egypt. Her curatorial work has also included collaborations with BOZAR – Centre for Fine Arts (Belgium), Cittadellarte – Fondazione Pistoletto (Italy), Institut français d’Égypte (Egypt), Mucem (France), Onassis Stegi (Greece), Medrar for Contemporary Art (Egypt), and Bsarya for Arts (Egypt), among others. Her artistic work has been exhibited internationally across Cairo, Beirut, Athens, Milan, Madrid, Bergen, Mexico City, Riyadh, Dubai, Casablanca, and the United States.
Benhalim holds an Alternative MA in Food & Art from The Gramounce (Spain), an MFA in Studio Art from Southern Methodist University (USA), and a BA in Visual Arts from The American University in Cairo.

people.biography:
Matthew Neff is an experienced global product leader with over 16 years in Product and Technology, including nearly 8 years in senior leadership roles within on-demand marketplaces. His career spans work across 30+ countries with some of the world’s most recognized platforms, including SkipTheDishes (Canada), Just Eat & Takeaway.com (Europe & Australia), and Rappi (LATAM).
At SkipTheDishes, Matthew joined when the company was handling 300,000 weekly orders and helped scale it to more than 2 million per week — a growth of nearly 700% during his tenure. At Just Eat / Takeaway.com, he served as Global Head of Operations Product, launching and scaling delivery services across multiple European markets and Australia, which grew to represent around 50% of the company’s order volume. At Rappi, Matthew spent 2.5 years as Director of Customer Product, where his team led multiple initiatives that drove a 6x improvement in Unit Economics and strengthened the company’s path to sustainable growth.
Today, as Chief Product Officer at Snoonu, Qatar’s pioneering super app, Matthew leads a team of product managers and designers to deliver innovations across food delivery, groceries, retail, events, and lifestyle services. He enjoys being a builder of products and tools that make people’s lives better and more convenient.

people.biography:
Mobola da-Silva is a Partner at Capria Ventures and is instrumental in driving Capria’s investment strategy in Africa and achieving the firm’s vision and growth ambition across the Global South.  A careful listener and a thoughtful strategist with an innate sense for value, Mobola has spent the last 20+ years of her career working with businesses, from start-ups to central banks, as an investor, as a consultant, and as an advisor.  With a wealth of experience in early-stage investing, she has a deep understanding of the African entrepreneurial landscape and a passion for supporting the incredible potential and innovation emerging from the continent. 

Before joining Capria, Mobola was a partner at the uMunthu Fund where she invested in technology-enabled businesses, providing access to essential goods and services for low to middle-income households in Africa. During her time at Alitheia Capital, she channeled smart capital into key growth sectors and wore multiple hats in the entrepreneurial environment of an emerging fund manager. 

Mobola has actively participated in advancing Africa’s investment ecosystem, collaborating with other stakeholders to birth Nigeria’s first formal angel investing network. She has held portfolio and non-portfolio-related non-executive director (NED) positions on company boards and is a portfolio advisor for the Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation.

Mobola holds an undergraduate degree from the University of Houston and an MBA from the University of Texas at Austin. She is also a London Business School Sloan Fellow with an MSc in Leadership and Strategy.

Mohab Eltawila is a sports entrepreneur and Founder & CEO of InGame Sports, an innovative football gaming platform redefining sports entertainment across the MENA region.

His journey combines specialized sports education, professional football experience, and large-scale sports management. Mohab began his football career in Al Ahly’s youth academy before playing NCAA Division I soccer in the United States. He holds an MBA from the Real Madrid Graduate School (Universidad Europea de Madrid) and a Bachelor’s degree in Sports Business from Northern Kentucky University.

Professionally, Mohab managed the iconic Pepsi Schools League, one of the world’s largest grassroots football initiatives, engaging over 1 million young players and famously discovering Mohamed Salah. He later founded Nogoom Football Club, leading the team to compete in the Egyptian Premier League in 2019.

Today, Mohab is building InGame as a next-generation sports venture for the region, transforming fans from passive spectators into active competitors through technology, gamification, and community. With deep expertise in sports business, product innovation, and emerging markets, he is passionate about shaping the future of football entertainment in the Middle East.

محمد أبو النجا "نجاتي" هو منشئ مشاريع في الأسواق الناشئة ومستثمر ورجل أعمال فى مجال التكنولوجيا  يتمتع بخبرة 15 عامًا في  مجال ريادة الأعمال التكنولوجية .
 
يشغل ابو النجا حاليًا منصب الرئيس التنفيذي ل” Exits “ أول منصة مصرفية استثمارية في مجال التكنولوجيا المالية في المنطقة ومؤسس ومدير تنفيذي لشركة” Pie “ الرائدة فى استشارات للشركات الناشئة في مصر"M and A".
 
يعد نجاتى شريك مؤسس في Cashcows (الذي يعتبر أكبر محفز للشركات الناشئة في مصر) و Mumerz  و ومستشار العلاقات العامة والحكومية في Disruptech (أكبر صندوق للتكنولوجيا المالية في مصر).
 
كذلك الشريك المؤسس لـ حالا ، حالا هو أكبر تطبيق سوبر في إفريقيا والأكثر تمويلًا في مصرعام 2020 وفقًا لـ Forbes Middle East ، والأكثر تمويلًا  حتى  عام 2022.
 
قبل مشاركته في تأسيس حالا ، شغل نجاتي منصب المدير الإقليمي في Careem، وهو التطبيق الأول في الشرق الأوسط الذي استحوذت عليه أوبر مؤخرا مقابل أكثر من 3 مليارات دولار.
كما أنه عضو في مجلس إدارة العديد من شركات التكنولوجيا بما في ذلك Koinz و Robusta و Waffarha و Checkme ومستثمر في العديد من الشركات الناشئة في مجال التكنولوجيا بما في ذلك Swype و Gameball و Sharwa و Sokna و ElGameya وغيرها من الشركات الأخرى في وقت سابق
 
بدأ نجاتي حياته المهنية في فوري في إدارة الحسابات وتطوير الأعمال منذ عام 2012 حتى ترأس BD ، كانت فوري أول شركة تكنولوجيا تطرح أسهمها في مصر وبلغت قيمتها 2 مليار دولار في الأسواق العامة) بالإضافة إلى بدء أول صندوق للأغذية والمشروبات في مصر في عام 2010 .
 
أكمل نجاتي برنامج أكاديمية CXO في INSEAD فرنسا ، وبكالوريوس في هندسة الإلكترونيات من الجامعة الأمريكية في القاهرة بمصر

people.biography:
I am Mohamed Alaa, a purpose-driven entrepreneur committed to reshaping the future of mental health, economic collaboration, and social development across the Middle East, Africa, and beyond. As the CEO of Shezlong, I’ve led the region’s first and largest online therapy platform serving millions of people across 85 countries and proving that innovation can heal, empower, and unite.

A Mission Beyond Business

My work goes beyond entrepreneurship.It’s a movement for humanity.
From empowering over 850 mental health professionals, to helping corporates and hospitals adopt digital wellness, to delivering accessible care for underserved communities, I’ve witnessed how mental well-being is the foundation of stronger economies, safer societies, and fulfilled lives.

Developing an AI-powered self-help platform that will make mental wellness a daily routine transforming care from reactive to proactive, and empowering individuals with tools to thrive.

But my mission doesn’t stop at health.

A Vision for Global Impact

I am deeply passionate about policy-making, economic diplomacy, and building bridges between nations. I believe in South-South cooperation, where countries of the Global South rise together through shared investments, innovation, and cultural understanding.

I actively contribute to efforts that:
	•	Foster economic cooperation across emerging markets
	•	Create investment opportunities that uplift communities
	•	Lead humanitarian and economic diplomatic missions focused on unity, progress, and inclusive development
	•	Champion cross-border collaboration for mental health, women’s empowerment, and social resilience

By 2030: A Bold Future

I will end silent suffering.
I will help build a world where mental wellness is accessible to all, stigma is obsolete, and innovation uplifts the most vulnerable.
A world where nations come together not only for trade or technology but for a better humanity.

A Talent with Vision and Responsibility

Internationally awarded and regionally rooted, I bring to the region a unique blend of entrepreneurial excellence, policy insight, and a human-centered vision for the future. I am proud to align my mission with the global leadership in innovation, sustainability, and global cooperation.

This is more than a personal journey. It’s a global commitment.

people.biography:
Mohamed F. Ahmed leads the GenAI Innovation and Delivery Startup Practice at AWS, where his team works with ambitious GenAI startups to help them scale from prototype to production. They focus on solving real infrastructure challenges—the kind that can make or break a startup navigating the economics of AI.

Before AWS, Mo was a serial entrepreneur with multiple ventures under his belt, including a successful exit that delivered a 7x return. Those years building companies taught him what founders actually need: not just infrastructure, but partners who understand the brutal realities of unit economics, burn rates, and the constant tension between moving fast and building for scale.

Mo holds a PhD in Computer Science and has held leadership roles at both Microsoft and Amazon, which gave him a deep appreciation for how technology and business strategy intersect in fast-moving markets like AI.

He’s the author of “The Inside-Out Entrepreneur,” where he shares lessons from his entrepreneurial journey. Over the years, he’s spoken at 100+ events globally on startups, AI, and innovation, energized by conversations with founders who are pushing boundaries and challenging conventional wisdom.

sessions.title: Stop Chatting, Start Acting: The Rise of Agentic AI
sessions.description: We are moving beyond Large Language Models that simply answer questions and entering the age of Agentic AI, systems capable of reasoning, planning, and executing complex workflows autonomously. In this session, we gather industry leaders to discuss how AI is transitioning from a passive consultant to an active workforce participant. We will explore how autonomous agents are redefining efficiency in different sectors.

people.biography:
Will it get me out of bed every morning, motivated and excited? Will it drive from inside and keep me pushing forward? Those are some of the questions I ask myself every single time before I embark on a new endeavor. And boy, I was lucky enough throughout my career journey so far!
What do I like the most about my career in communications?
Interacting with people and listening to their stories. Every person is unique in their own way, and that is what makes every story distinctive. My job is to shed light on the untold stories, bring them to life, and share them with the world.
Sounds fascinating, isn't it? That's because it truly is a humbling and enriching experience.
A team player? You bet! Working together as a team on different projects is one of the best parts I enjoy in my role. It's like a melting pot of creativity and ideas that comes out of that. I am super proud that I was part of the team that developed and executed the media awareness campaign for the Sustainable Development Strategy: Egypt Vision 2030 and spearheaded the outreach activities for the Integrity Network Initiative- a collective effort to fight corruption and create an efficient and enabling business environment.
I get excited about opportunities where l'm able to work with highly creative people and generate a real-world impact. It seems I tend to push myself outside of my comfort zone to feel that adrenaline rush over and over.
I might not have all the answers, but I hope I can ask the right questions.
Core focuses of interest currently include external communications, internal communications, employer branding, public relations, event management, sustainability, and technology.

people.biography:
I’m the Co-Founder and Chief Strategy Officer at Mezatech, a tech services group focused on repair, refurbishment, and building sustainable tech solutions across Egypt and the MENA region.

My journey didn’t start in a boardroom—it started with a screwdriver. I spent years working hands-on in device diagnostics and repair, and that experience shaped how I think about teams, products, and execution. Over time, I moved into leadership roles, building operations, scaling teams, and turning technical work into repeatable, scalable businesses.

I’m Apple Certified in Technical Support and Huawei Certified in Smart Device Repair. Today, a big part of my focus is BlackMint, Mezatech’s refurbished devices platform, where we’re making premium tech more accessible while extending device lifecycles and reducing e-waste.

At RiseUp, I’ll be sharing real lessons from building my first teams—what worked, what failed, and what I wish I knew earlier. No theory, no buzzwords—just practical insights on hiring, defining roles, setting clear ownership, and scaling without losing quality or culture.

And yes—I do enjoy long walks, especially when they come with big ideas and good conversations.

people.biography:
Mohamed Okasha is the Founder and Managing Partner of Disruptech Ventures. He serves as the Chairman of the Investment Committee and represents the Fund on the Board of Directors of some of the portfolio companies including Mozare3, Sprints, and Bokra.

Okasha was recently selected to be a member of the Prime Minister’s Advisory Committee for Entrepreneurship and Digital Transformation.

Okasha is a seasoned executive and thought leader with over 30 years of experience. Most recently, Mohamed was a co-founder and Managing Director of Fawry, Egypt’s leading e-payments company. Okasha co-founded the company in 2009 and led it through multiple funding rounds till its successful IPO in 2019, taking the company value to over $2 billion.

Prior to founding Fawry, Okasha served as the Head of Marketing at Vodafone Egypt, where he led several business operations.

Okasha started his career at Raya Holding, where he spent 10 years in several of the group’s subsidiaries until he became the General Manager of the IT subsidiary.'

Okasha holds a B.Sc. in Computer Science from the American University in Cairo, and an MBA from the ESLSCA Business School Paris. In addition to completing the Management Development Program at the IMD Business School.

people.biography:
Mohamed Omar is the Strategic Partner Manager for Established Talents at Meta, where he has spent nearly seven years building partnerships with leading entertainment voices across the Middle East and North Africa. He works closely with actors, musicians, and cultural figures to help them tell stories that shape how the region is seen globally. His role combines creative collaboration, product insight, and long term relationship building.

Before Meta, Mohamed spent three years at X as a content partnerships consultant for entertainment, news, media, and sports. He previously served as Editor in Chief of FilFan.com at Sarmady and worked as an entertainment editor in print tabloids, covering many of the Arab world’s biggest stars and cultural moments. He holds a bachelor’s degree in History from Cairo University.

people.biography:
I founded Benchmark Consumer Products (BCP) not simply to start a company, but to give form to a long-held vision. What began as a personal ambition has evolved into one of Egypt’s fastest-growing platforms in cosmetics, beauty, and perfumery.

From the outset, my leadership has been driven by a belief that enduring brands are built at the intersection of creativity, discipline, and deep consumer understanding. I have led BCP’s transformation into an influential industry player, anchored in a clear mission: to craft exceptional products that elevate everyday experiences, exceed consumer expectations, and build lasting partnerships across the value chain.

My core expertise lies in building businesses and brands from the ground up—pioneering market strategies, architecting growth models, and leading product development. This approach has enabled the creation of a diversified brand portfolio, scaled through strong multi-channel distribution and expanding export markets. Through strategic collaborations and innovation-led execution, I have driven sustained revenue growth and increasing market recognition.

Beyond growth, my focus has been on shaping a culture of reliability, bold thinking, and uncompromising execution. This foundation has allowed BCP to consistently translate vision into tangible market impact—launching distinctive brands, entering new categories, and moving with agility in a rapidly evolving industry.

Today, I continue to lead Benchmark Consumer Products with a long-term ambition: to build a globally relevant consumer products house from the region—one that creates brands of substance, earns trust at scale, and leaves a meaningful imprint on the future of beauty, fragrance, and personal care.

people.biography:
Monica Brand Engel is a co-founder and Managing Partner at Quona Capital, a venture firm focused on fintech for inclusion in emerging markets. As an entrepreneur and investor, Monica has launched various funds and products aimed at broadening financial inclusion. At Quona, she leads EMEA + Global investments. Backed by leading institutional investors, Quona manages $800 million of assets across a portfolio of funds backing pioneering founders who are scaling inclusive fintech. 
Monica’s career began in Silicon Valley, where she helped launch a $50 million multi-bank lending intermediary to finance small businesses. She has also worked at Calvert Ventures and Anthuri Ventures, early-stage equity vehicles in Bethesda and Cape Town, respectively. While in South Africa, Monica founded Anthuri Catalysts to prepare early-stage companies for investment. 
Recruited by Accion to spearhead product innovation, Monica worked with retail financial institutions globally including a secondment to Mexico with Gentera Bank (née Compartamos). At the time, Latin America’s largest microfinance institution, Compartamos went public in 2007 (NSDQ: GENTERA). Using the IPO proceeds, she founded Accion’s Frontier Investments Group, the predecessor to Quona Capital.
Monica holds an MBA and MA in Education from Stanford University and a BA in economics from Williams College. She serves on the boards of Khazna, Maxsoko, Verto, and Twinco and is a founding member of the GPCA Impact Council. Her previous board positions include Yoco, Gentera Bank (IPO), Shubham Housing (sold to Premji Invest), Pay Rent Builds Credit (acquired by MicroBilt), Tiaxa (acquired by BeMobi), Azimo (acquired by Papaya), Zoona (acquired by Chipper Cash). She also chaired the Investor Representative Committee of LeapFrog I, the world’s first dedicated microinsurance fund. 
Monica has (co-)authored and contributed to various printed publications on product development (Technical Note and Field Guide Synthesis), financial inclusion (Maximizing Efficiency and Transforming Microfinance Institutions), impact investing (New Frontiers of Philanthropy) and most recently, women in leadership (Rebalance: How Women Lead, Parent, Partner … and Thrive).  
Monica is half Peruvian and blessed with a fantastic husband and twins.

people.biography:
Mostafa Salem is an Egyptian architect, urban thinker, and founder of Coconut, a Dubai-based architecture and interior design studio operating across the MENA region. His work focuses on the intersection of architecture, heritage preservation, sustainability, and public impact, with a strong emphasis on human-centered and context-driven design.

Salem is best known for the Cairo Makeover initiative, a research-based urban intervention series that reimagines historic districts such as Downtown Cairo through walkability, façade restoration, and adaptive reuse. The initiative has significantly influenced public awareness and discourse around architecture and heritage in Egypt, reaching millions across digital platforms.

He has represented Egypt in major international platforms, including the Venice Biennale, and has received 14 national and international awards, among them the Egyptian State Encouragement Award and the Arab Creativity Award. In 2025, he was selected by Apostrophe S Magazine as Best Architect of the Year for his cultural and professional influence, and was named on Cairo Scene’s Impact List, recognizing the most impactful figures shaping contemporary Egypt.

Salem has delivered two TED Talks and has spoken at leading international events and forums, including GITEX and public talks in Paris. Alongside practice, he is an active lecturer and mentor, advocating for architecture that moves beyond trends and social-media aesthetics toward lasting cultural, social, and environmental value.

people.biography:
Muhannad Ebwini
Founder & CEO, HyperPay
Muhannad Ebwini is the Founder and CEO of HyperPay, a leading online payment solutions provider headquartered in Saudi Arabia. Under his visionary leadership, HyperPay has grown into one of the Middle East’s fastest-growing and most successful digital payment businesses, recognized for its innovation and its role as a new-generation payment service provider.
HyperPay is the second certified online payment solution provider in Saudi Arabia as an eMSP – Payment Gateway (PG) by Saudi Payments. In 2017, Muhannad was also appointed as a board member of GatetoPay, a prominent card issuing company that provides prepaid MasterCard, Visa, and UnionPay card solutions across the Middle East region.
With over 25 years of experience in FinTech, eCommerce, gaming, and payments industries, Muhannad has been a driving force in shaping the region’s digital economy. His leadership is marked by the ability to build high-performing teams, forge strategic partnerships, and inspire innovation. At OneCard, he spearheaded the growth of the company (2004–2010), playing a pioneering role in developing the online payment and eCommerce ecosystem across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). He worked with international and regional players to adapt solutions for the MENA market, while also introducing value-added services such as customer support centers and marketing initiatives.
Prior to OneCard, Muhannad served as Business Development Manager of Souq.com (formerly an online auction service at Maktob, later acquired by Yahoo and transformed into the MENA region’s largest eCommerce platform). Earlier in his career, he held leadership roles in sales and marketing at eSolution, a web development company in Amman, Jordan.
Muhannad is widely recognized as a forward-thinking leader who combines deep industry expertise with a strong commitment to advancing digital transformation across the Middle East. His ability to scale businesses, mentor talent, and drive cross-border collaboration has made him a key influencer in the FinTech ecosystem.
He is a Certified eCommerce Consultant (CEC) and Project Manager eBusiness (PME), holding an MBA in Management and International Business from NYIT (New York Institute of Technology) and a BSc in Computer Software Engineering from Princess Sumaya University in Amman, Jordan.

As a JICA Expert for Innovation and Startup Ecosystems, he previously supported national digital innovation initiatives under the Nigerian government and is currently focused on advancing Egypt’s startup ecosystem. His work centers on facilitating collaboration and co-creation between Japanese corporations and African startups, working closely with public agencies, corporates, and investors to drive innovation and international partnerships.

He began his career in the capital markets division of an investment bank, later serving as a managing director of a tech startup, before joining JICA and working in Uganda, Ethiopia, and Nigeria. He holds an M.A. in Financial Mathematics from Boston University.

people.biography:
Norah Abokhodair, PhD is the Head of Upskilling & AI Transformation for International Public Sector at Scale AI. She leads global efforts to move AI learning from theory to practice by embedding hands-on, applied training directly into real-world deployments across governments, universities, and startup ecosystems.

Norah’s work focuses on building future-ready, AI-literate talent that can design, govern, and scale AI systems with long-term ownership, enabling institutions and founders to shape and own their AI future rather than outsource it. She holds a PhD in Information Science from the University of Washington and is a Fulbright alum. Prior to Scale AI, Norah led AI-powered products at Microsoft, working at the intersection of product strategy, machine learning, and responsible AI. She is also the founder of Siyadah AI and a frequent advisor and speaker on applied AI, public-sector innovation, and ecosystem development.

people.biography: Nour Taher is the CEO and co-founder of Intella, a leading Arabic-first AI company building voice and text intelligence solutions for regional dialects and cultural nuance. She is on a mission to make advanced AI accessible, relevant, and impactful for Arabic-speaking markets. Nour has received multiple international accolades, including the Women in Tech Award (MENA 2023), first place at the She Loves Tech Middle East Regional Competition, and third place at the She Loves Tech Global Summit in Singapore (2024). She was also the regional champion of the Startup World Cup, representing the only MENA-based company to reach the semifinals in Silicon Valley. A graduate of Western University, Nour holds a double major in Business Management and Psychology, a combination that strongly informs her product vision and leadership style. Beyond her role at Intella, she serves as an advisory board member at Peleset Angels Network, where she supports and mentors Palestinian entrepreneurs. Driven by a belief in inclusive innovation, Nour continues to champion the development of AI solutions that reflect the language, culture, and realities of the Arab world.

people.biography:
Omar Heraiz is a creative strategist, educator, and co-founder of SYNC, a platform operating at the intersection of creative education, industry insight, and talent development in the MENA region.

With over 12 years of hands-on experience across content creation, filmmaking, brand storytelling, and creative direction, Omar has worked closely with creatives, agencies, startups, and corporates to understand how creative work actually functions once it leaves the moodboard and hits reality. His work spans building education programs, curating large-scale creative summits, designing career pathways, and developing future-focused content platforms.


Omar is particularly interested in how creativity behaves under pressure - when budgets shrink, automation accelerates, and job titles dissolve - and how creative thinking evolves from a “nice to have” into a survival skill. He likes challenging surface-level narratives around passion and talent, pushing instead for adaptability, strategic thinking, and creative literacy as long-term career assets.

sessions.title: Creativity Under Pressure

people.biography:
Radwa Moussa-Youssef is a 43-year-old Egyptian-American mother of three, real estate entrepreneur, and passionate childhood cancer advocate. At her core, she’s a storyteller—someone who loves meaningful conversations, discovering new places, and connecting to people through music and shared experiences.

She co-founded the Southern California–based non-profit Create a Smile, where for over eight years she has supported children battling cancer, all while building and managing a successful real estate business.

Her debut book, Zein: When Nothing Is Sure – Everything Is Possible, courageously addresses cancer stigma and became a Middle East bestseller, touching thousands of families with its honesty and hope.

In 2024, Radwa launched her podcast نقطة و من اول السطر, a space for raw, unfiltered conversations about resilience, transformation, identity, and the beauty of starting over, often inspired by her own journey between East and West.

As a public speaker and community advocate, Radwa uses her voice to spark dialogue around social issues, parenting, and women’s empowerment, showing up authentically online and offline, always curious, always listening, and always evolving.

sessions.title: From Launch to Growth: Building a Podcast

people.biography:
Sadaharu Saiki(a.k.a. Sada), Founder & General Partner at Sunny Side Venture Partners, based in Cairo, Egypt, is passionate about finding startups with good ambitions and supporting them in scaling their businesses & their impact into the world. He worked at Dentsu Inc., one of the largest marketing and advertising companies in the world, for 6 years in Tokyo, Japan, mainly serving Toyota’s global marketing team, and 3 years in Bangalore, India, engaging in helping Japanese multinational corporations expand in India, before he went to study at Harvard Business School(HBS). At HBS, he was a VP of Africa Business Club and a member of Impact Investing Club and Consulting for Impact Club. While at HBS, he worked at Kepple Africa Ventures, a VC in Kenya and Working Capital Fund, an Omidyar Network-affiliated impact VC in Washington D.C. After graduating with distinction, he joined McKinsey & Company, and in 2022, founded Sunny Side Venture Partners, the first Asian VC based in North Africa. Sunny Side Venture Partners targets early-stage startups across Africa and the Middle East. It has so far invested in 24 companies operating across 24 countries. He is an active supporter and advocator of the local ecosystem, having participated and spoken so far at 70+ startup related conferences/events for Africa & the Middle East across 22 cities in 15 countries, including Japan-India-Africa Business Forum organized by Nikkei and METI in Tokyo, Japan, Global Startup Expo in Osaka, Japan(A official side event of Expo 2025), GITEX Africa in Marrakech, Morocco(Africa’s largest startup conference), RiseUp Summit in Cairo, Egypt(Egypt’s largest startup conference), etc.

Sadaharu holds a Bachelor in Integrated Human Studies from Kyoto University and a Master in Business Administration (MBA) with Distinction[Top 10% of the entire cohort] from Harvard Business School.

sessions.title: Why Global Investors are Looking at Africa?

people.biography:
Sarah Abouelkhair is an architect, designer, and creative entrepreneur with a Master’s degree in Advanced Architectural Design from Columbia University and a Bachelor's degree in Architecture from the American University in Cairo (AUC). 
Her passion for design, storytelling, and social interaction led her to co-found 2oolameme in 2020 alongside Abdelrahman Khaled. The company quickly became a cultural phenomenon, known for creating Egypt’s most iconic social games. Under her creative leadership, 2oolameme has sold over 1 million games, launched 24 original IPs, partnered with brands such as TikTok, Dell, and Allianz, and built a strong presence both in physical retail and through its mobile gaming platform, Kooz, which now has over 400,000 active users.
Sarah’s work blends humor, cultural insight, and design thinking. Her company was awarded the “Art to Business” prize at the 2024 EEAwards, and she was named on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list, as continues to push boundaries at the intersection of play, creativity, and cultural relevance.

sessions.title: From Idea to Game: How Card and Board Games Are Created

Sarah’s work blends humor, cultural insight, and design thinking. Her company was awarded the “Art to Business” prize at the 2024 EEAwards, and she was named on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list, as continues to push boundaries at the intersection of play, creativity, and cultural relevance.

Shadi El Ghoneimi is a French-Egyptian architect with over 20 years of experience specializing in hospitality design. He currently leads El Ghoneimi International, a family-owned firm founded in 1983, continuing its legacy of innovative and avant-garde design tailored to the evolving hospitality industry.

Shadi earned his Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees from the École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture Paris-La Seine (Les Beaux-Arts de Paris) and is a member of the Ordre des Architectes Français (Île-de-France) as well as the Egyptian Union of Architects.

Throughout his career, Shadi has directed the design of a diverse array of notable hospitality projects across the EMEA region, collaborating with leading international brands such as Marriott, Hilton, Accor, and IHG.

Born and raised in Cairo and educated in Paris, Shadi’s design philosophy is deeply influenced by these two vibrant cities. He is passionate about creating timeless spaces that seamlessly blend multicultural aesthetics with operational functionality, ensuring each project reflects its unique historical context and a strong sense of place.

people.biography:
Surayyah Ahmad is currently the Taskmaster spearheading the operationalisation
of the Youth Entrepreneurship Investment Bank (YEIB Investment Funds)—a $300m
blended capital vehicle conceptualised by the AfDB and co-owned by the NSIA and
Development Bank of Nigeria. YEIB aims to provide financial and technical
assistance to youth-led enterprises in Nigeria through wholesale and retail
financing. Surayyah is also a Founding Partner at Sabou Capital (formerly Aduna
Capital), which provides funding and technical support to high-growth SMEs in
West and Central Africa with a gender lens. She supports UK scale-ups through her
role as a scale-up advisor at Barclays Eagle Labs. Additionally, she sits on multiple
startup advisory boards and chairs the Laidlaw Foundation Women in Business
Board.
Surayyah has an MBA from the University of Oxford, specialising in finance and
impact investing. She also served as co-chair of the Oxford Africa Business Alliance,
working to foster engagement between Oxford’s business community and the
African continent.
As an experienced operator, Surayyah founded and successfully exited an e-
commerce and fulfilment service company with operations in both Nigeria and the
UK. She is deeply passionate about empowering women and driving economic
development in underserved markets through private enterprise and investment.

people.biography:
Susana Garcia-Robles is a recognized expert on entrepreneurship, high-impact investment, building diversified VC ecosystems, and an investor in applied AI startups and VC funds. She is a Managing Partner at Capria Ventures, responsible for the Middle East, Africa, and LATAM regions. She recently led the final close of the firm’s second fund for the Global South and is now researching strategies built on Capria’s deep global south capabilities for the firm’s next funds for Latin America and Africa.

Before joining Capria, she served as Chief Investment Officer and Gender Initiatives Coordinator at the Inter-American Development Bank. She was the leading architect of its investment strategy for early-stage funds and startups from 19990-2020. She is also a Senior Advisor, a member of the Women’s Council and a former Board member of the Association for Private Capital Investment in Latin America (LAVCA).

An avid supporter of ecosystems, she co-founded the Argentine VC/PE Association/ARCAP and the Colombian VC/PE Association/Colcapital. She served on the Advisory Boards of the Brazilian VC/PE association /ABVCAP, the Board of Directors of Village Capital (2020-2023), and currently serves on the Advisory Board of the Argentinean VC/PE association/ARCAP, the CITES company builder/fund, the IgnitXL fund, the IThink VC fund, as well as in the investment committee of the Bancoldex Fund of Funds (Colombia) and the Fondo de Capital para Emprendimientos Innovadores (Peruvian Fund of Funds from COFIDE).

In 2012, she co-founded Wexchange (now housed at IDB), the first networking platform and pitch competition for LAC women STEMpreneurs, dramatically improving women’s access to funding. She also cofounded EmprendedorasLAC. In 2019, she co-founded WeInvest Latam, a platform for women investors with LATAM as the central focus region.

A recognized expert on development finance innovation, Susana has analyzed and coached thousands of seed and VC funds and startup founders and invested $500M in over 100 funds, startups. and ecosystem building programs. She’s now transferring her knowledge and experience building the VC industry in LATAM to other places in the Global South, mainly Africa and the Middle East. Through her work with Capria’s portfolio, she has developed expertise on applying Generative AI to startups across the Global South to increase profitability, expand TAMs, and build defensible “data moats” that are critical for survival in a fast-moving market.

For her pioneering work in LATAM and efforts to make the VC industry more inclusive, she has been dubbed “the godmother of VC in LAC.” Americas Quarterly recognized her as one of the five 2020 Top Champions on Gender Equality. She has also been recognised by LAVCA as a Top Woman Investor in Latin America — every year, for nine years, from 2016 to 2024.

Susana has master’s degrees in Philosophy and Education from the Universidad Catolica of Argentina, and in International Relations, concentrating on International Economic Policies from Columbia University.

Currently, she lives in Virginia with her husband, Daniel Q. Kelley, visits her sister in Buenos Aires as often as she can, and is very close to her other sister and her family, also residing in Virginia.

people.biography:
With over 20 years of experience in international trade negotiations, export strategy, and trade policy, Tamer Mahmoud has worked at the intersection of government, development, and the private sector, helping stakeholders navigate complex trade frameworks and translate them into sustainable economic growth. He served as Manager of the Regional Agreements Department at the Ministry of Industry and Foreign Trade, where he played a central role in advising on and shaping Egypt’s regional and international trade policies. He is currently the Chief Executive Officer of TRAIN, a capacity-building company supporting businesses in accessing and growing in international markets.

Tamer has contributed to the design, negotiation, and implementation of major trade frameworks, including GAFTA, COMESA, AfCFTA, the EU–Egypt Association Agreement, and the Tripartite Trade Negotiation Forum (COMESA–SADC–EAC). He has represented Egypt in numerous high-level international negotiations, led Egypt’s delegation on Rules of Origin, and chaired key committees at the League of Arab States, including the Arab Customs Union Committee and the Arab Rules of Origin Committee. Building on this experience, he now supports businesses and trade institutions in leveraging these agreements to expand into new markets and strengthen their competitive positioning.

Tamim El Zein is a co-founder and General Partner at Seedstars Africa Ventures, an early-stage venture capital fund leading pre-Series A and Series A investment rounds across Africa. 
An entrepreneur at heart, Tamim has been on both sides of the table throughout his career. Before co-founding Seedstars Africa Ventures, he was himself an entrepreneur in Africa, experiencing firsthand the operational and financial challenges facing founders on the continent. He previously served as COO of a high-growth tech startup in Europe, where he gained deep insights into scaling technology businesses. 
His entrepreneurial background shapes his investment philosophy, emphasizing hands-on operational support alongside capital. Tamim began his career as a strategy consultant specializing in innovation and telecommunications across the Middle East and Africa region. He later joined the strategy team of a world-leading company in B2B payment solutions, authentication, and identity services, where he led VC and M&A deals as an investor, gaining expertise in fintech infrastructure and cross-border transactions. 
Bilingual in French and English, Tamim is particularly active on bridging the funding gap in francophone Africa. He serves as a regular mentor with leading programs and is a sought-after speaker at major industry forums.

people.biography:
Toufic Kreidieh is the Executive Chairman of the Board and Group
CEO of the BFL Group - one of the leading off-price retailers in
the Middle East and Europe. With his extensive commercial and
retail experience, he has steered the BFL Group to
tremendous success, with over 100 branches spread across
the region.
Kreidieh began his career as an administrator in Saudi Arabia where he managed two jobs
simultaneously. Kreidieh learned the importance of hard work and commitment at a young age and coins
his success to the values gained during those early days. Being a seasonal speaker who delivers
keynote speeches with great enthusiasm, Kreidieh enjoys connecting with people, whether it is with staff,
business partners, customers or with aspiring entrepreneurs. His success story is inspiring for young
entrepreneurs and a reminder that there are no shortcuts to success.
Kreidieh is an experienced keynote speaker and advisor who enjoys building a connection with his
team members, as well as aspiring business owners. He actively encourages his audience to support
others in achieving their goals and enhancing their skill sets. Kreidieh has always been committed to
giving back to the community and supports several CSR projects. He strongly believes in projects
that support the advancement of social change, art & culture and small businesses. Among other
initiatives, he has supported the educational needs of students through a collaboration with
the universities, which led to a donations of over USD 1,000,000. Over the years, BFL Group
has partnered with various charitable organisations such as: ‘Dar El Berr’, ‘Dubai Cares’ and the
‘Emirates Red Crescent Society’.
Kreidieh’s passion for business has allowed him to implement remarkable innovations across the BFL
Group. He is a firm believer in the importance of leveraging creativity and technology to deliver the
utmost results.

people.biography:
My name is Venus El Rayes , a Cairo-based MC, PR consultant, photographer, and the founder of From Venus With Love Studio, my creative sanctuary where storytelling, visuals, and human connection all come together.

I didn’t start in the creative world; I actually began as a civil engineer. But somewhere between construction sites and corporate life, I realized my real passion was people, stories, and the energy of bringing ideas to life. So I shifted paths, boldly  and built a career shaped by culture, creativity, and community.

Today, I work across Egypt’s most exciting spaces: from Art D’Égypte Design Week ,and FI Africa to SwissCham Egypt, UFI MEA, and major summits centered on innovation, design, sustainability, and the business of art. I love being on stage ,hosting, moderating, and turning conversations into experiences people actually feel. I bring warmth, clarity, and a spark of humor to every audience I meet.

Photography is another part of my world. At From Venus With Love Studio, I focus on capturing real energy , portraits that feel alive, brand stories rooted in authenticity, and moments that show people as they truly are. My style is bright, bold, and intuitive. I don’t just take images; I build visual narratives.

Everything I do is built on one mission, to connect people, elevate ideas, and create moments that stay with you.

I’m driven by curiosity, learning , inspired by human stories, and always ready for the next project that lets me mix creativity with impact.

people.biography:
Victoria Caña is a game production leader at The Pokémon Company International, where she helps bring the Pokémon digital card game to life. She’s also the co-founder and designer at Cat Quartet Games, the indie studio behind the Kickstarter hit Gladius and the party game Hot Takes.

Her career is an adventure through some of the biggest names in games, including Riot Games, Wizards of the Coast, and Probably Monsters, where she’s worked on everything from experimental R&D projects to global favorites like Legends of Runeterra and Magic: The Gathering. Before entering game development, she was a management consultant at Deloitte, helping Fortune 500 companies navigate major changes—experience that still comes in handy when shipping ambitious games.

Victoria is a passionate speaker who loves connecting with creative communities. She’s spoken at San Diego Comic-Con, PAX, and conferences around the world, always bringing her enthusiasm for games, strategy, and storytelling to the stage.

When she’s not making games, you’ll likely find her traveling in search of amazing food, flowing through hot yoga, or dreaming up new worlds for her fantasy novel.

people.biography:
"Cici is an economist with a leading Multilateral Development Bank, with cross-regional expertise spanning Africa and the MENA region. She began working in Africa in 2022 as an Impact Fellow with LGT Venture Philanthropy based in Nairobi, where she contributed to the design of a catalytic fund focused on strengthening the continent’s primary health care systems. She is a recognized connector in the China-Africa entrepreneurship ecosystem, serving as an advisor to Roselake Ventures (the most active China-backed VC investing in Africa), Future Hub (Africa’s first Chinese-backed incubator supported by Transsion Group), and C Star Incubation (the largest Chinese incubator in Africa, funded by China Merchants Group).

Complementing her work in Africa, Cici also brings strategic experience from the MENA region. She served as an economic advisor to Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Communications and Information Technology on digital economy strategy.

Cici has further contributed to advancing China-Africa and China-MENA collaboration through her consulting work with the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, the Foreign Economic Cooperation Office of China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment, and leading academic institutions, private sector players, and civil society organizations.

Beyond her professional roles, she was selected as a Young Scholar by Research ICT Africa and currently serves on the member committee of the CFA Society East Africa. She is also part of the founding team of a new Africa-based business school. Additionally, Cici hosts a podcast featuring Chinese entrepreneurs and investors, which was recognized by Apple as the “Best Chinese Podcast of the Year.”"

people.biography:
William Bao Bean
Orbit Ventures - Managing General Partner

William is Managing General Partner of Orbit Ventures the Emerging Markets VC the longest running emerging market startup program in the world with over US$125m in investment value managed. Orbit invests in technology startups that digitize traditional industries, boost earnings potential, and drive sustainable growth. Sectors include ecommerce, fintech, travel, media, health, education, and logistics across emerging markets in Asia, Middle East, Africa and LATAM. Orbit provides hands-on support for user acquisition, sales, partnerships, and fundraising. Orbit's consumer ecosystem has helped our startups scale to 169m monthly active users as of 2Q25. Magnitt named Orbit #6 most active VC in Emerging Markets in both 2023, 2024 and 2H25. William joined Orbit from SingTel Innov8 Ventures where he was a founding Managing Director. Prior to that William was a Partner at Softbank China & India, a VC backed by Softbank and Cisco, leading investments across Asia. William started his career in equity research most recently with Deutsche Bank where he was a top ranked analyst for Internet and Software in Asia and worked on the IPOs for Alibaba, Kingsoft, eLong (Expedia), OnMobile and Infoedge Naukri.

William was ranked #3 stock picker in Hong Kong/China and #1 for Technology, Media and Telecom by Thomson Reuters Starmine as well as #3 equity research analyst in Asia for Software and IT Services by Institutional Investor Magazine. William has done over 350 early stage investments including Bitmex in blockchain, UShopal in ecommerce, italki in edtech, VideoVerse in media, Carota in mobility, Flickstree in media, ELSA Speak in edtech, Tappytoon in media, Coutloot in ecommerce, and Dastgyr in ecommerce.  He currently sits on boards including Scantrust, Boost Capital, Pandabus, Fleksy, Goama, and italki as well as Blair Academy. He holds a BA from Bowdoin College.

people.biography:
Yara studied product design and social business between Egypt and Germany. 
She always had passion in combining design and community, believing that change happens when both collide.Right after graduation, she worked for International Organization for Migration to empower women living in remote areas through product design. It’s this 7 month experience in a small village in Upper Egypt that proved her that she is only passionate about sustainability and women empowerment. Then in 2015 she co-founded Up-fuse ( which was her pre master project already in 2013). For 10 years now, Yara has been full timing at Up-fuse, co-growing it from a DIY Plastic bag recycling into a successful  business, supporting more than 80 artisanal women from the garbage city in Cairo. The business is not only raising environmental awareness but also helped in upcycling 3,350,000 plastic bags and counting.
 Yara has represented women from the Middle East in Several World bank Events. She was awarded by the UN Environment among 10 young women from around the world who help in a greener future.
Yara has represented Start-ups in Green business in OSCE 2019 conference to help support the allocation of budget for start-ups.
Yara is currently conducting a sustainble design fashion coursefor undergrad  students at the AUC.

people.biography:
Youssef Salem is CFO of ADX-listed ADNOC Drilling, world’s largest integrated driller; and Chair of Enersol, $1.5bn energy tech platform.
 
Youssef’s experience includes being CFO of AIQ, MENA’s first AI unicorn and now a subsidiary of ADX-listed Presight; CFO & Director at Nasdaq-listed Swvl, world’s first mass transit marketplace to go public; Executive Director & Senior Advisor at Moelis, executing >$150bn of capital raises and M&A; and Adjunct Professor of Practice at the American University in Cairo.
 
Youssef is also an Entrepreneur in Residence at Hub71. He is a CFA Charterholder and Fellow of the Society of Actuaries.

people.biography:
Zach is the Co-Founder and Managing Partner at Launch Africa Ventures - Africa's most prominent and active early-stage VC Fund with a portfolio of 160+ tech ventures across 25+ countries. He is also the Co-Founder and Chief Investment Officer of Startupbootcamp AfriTech – one of the leading multi-corporate backed venture accelerators program in Africa. 

Zach is a prominent Angel investor in 50+ leading tech startups in Africa including Flutterwave, KudaBank, Mono, Yoco and several others. He was featured on the cover of Fast Company (May 2018), Destiny Man (Nov 2019), Forbes (Aug 2023), and on several occasions on CNBC Africa. In 2020, he was recognized as one of the Top 4 Most Influential Persons in Technology in Africa by Les Echos (the French equivalent of the Financial Times). 

Zach was formerly the head of Africa Investments for U-Start – the largest network of private Multi-Family offices in Europe. Prior to moving to South Africa, he was an investment banker on Wall Street covering mergers & acquisitions, corporate finance strategy and risk management at Lehman Brothers and Barclays Capital, New York. 

Zach has a Master’s degree in Finance & Management from Stanford University and a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology. He is a member of MENSA International - the Global High IQ Society. 

Outside of his professional life, Zach is an acoustic guitarist, pianist and vocalist with  cover albums ‘Give A Little’ (2010) and ‘Humans with Hearts’ (2018) on iTunes and Spotify. He is an avid lover of theater and the performing arts, likes hiking and a good game of tennis and squash. He enjoys creative writing and is currently busy finishing a work of non-fiction.

people.biography:
Zuhair Khayyat is the CTO of a technology startup and a product-minded technologist with a passion for building systems that turn complex data into meaningful, human-centered experiences. Currently part of the engineering leadership at Lucidya, Zuhair works at the intersection of software development, AI-powered platforms, and scalable backend systems, helping organizations better understand and engage with their customers.

With a strong foundation in engineering and a curiosity that extends beyond code, Zuhair enjoys tackling challenging problems, shaping technical vision, and driving strategic decisions that support long-term growth. He believes that great technology is not only about performance and architecture, but also about empathy by understanding the people who use it and the impact it creates.

Outside of day-to-day execution, Zuhair is deeply interested in artificial intelligence, product strategy, and the evolving relationship between humans and technology. He enjoys learning new tools, experimenting with ideas, and staying close to the broader tech ecosystem, whether through conversations, reading, or hands-on exploration.

When he’s not focused on strategic long-term planning or aligning teams around a shared technical roadmap, you’ll likely find Zuhair enjoying long walks, reflecting on ideas, or seeking out good coffee and thoughtful discussions. He values collaboration, continuous growth, and environments that encourage curiosity and creativity.

sessions.title: Stop Chatting, Start Acting: The Rise of Agentic AI
sessions.description: We are moving beyond Large Language Models that simply answer questions and entering the age of Agentic AI, systems capable of reasoning, planning, and executing complex workflows autonomously. In this session, we gather industry leaders to discuss how AI is transitioning from a passive consultant to an active workforce participant. We will explore how autonomous agents are redefining efficiency in different sectors.
